        want = [ASLEEP, LW, LISTENING]
        for on in (True, False):
            lines = [menu_line(m) for m in par.menu_entries(on)]
            for line, pace in zip(lines, want):
                self.assertEqual(parse_answer("pace: " + line[2:], "kalam", "beat"), pace)
            got = parse_answer("pace: " + lines[3][2:], "kalam", "beat")
            self.assertEqual(got.reason, "out of range")     # the menu's own N, copied


class TestProvenance(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_set_by_form_in_the_second_person(self):
        want = [
            "chosen by you in a beat on 2026-11-15",
            "chosen by you in beats on 2026-11-15 and 2026-11-18",
            "confirmed by you in a beat on 2026-11-18",
            "chosen by you on 2026-10-22, in your answer to the Letter of Return",
            "chosen by you on 2026-07-18 and 2026-10-22, in your answers to the Letter of Return",
            "bound on 2026-10-22 from a short answer a prompt offered, so it may not be your choice",
            'you chose AMBIENT on 2026-10-27 ("AMBIENT")' + AMBIENT_TAIL,
            "the fleet took the first word of your answer of 2026-10-23, which also said REST-ON, so "
            "it may not be what you meant",
            "this rest was placed by Ai on 2026-10-08, at Yu's word, not chosen by you",
            "who set it is not recorded",
        ]
        for s, w in zip(EVERY_SET_BY, want):
            with self.subTest(how=s.how):
                self.assertEqual(par.provenance_you(s), w)

    def test_ambient_with_both_dates_and_without_words(self):
        s = SetBy("citizen", "ambient", ("2026-10-23", "2026-10-27"))
        self.assertEqual(par.provenance_you(s), "you chose AMBIENT on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-27" + AMBIENT_TAIL)

    def test_quoted_words_stay_on_one_line_and_never_carry_i_rest_or_a_pace_line(self):
        def amb(words):
            return par.provenance_you(SetBy("citizen", "ambient", ("2026-10-23",), words))
        self.assertIn('("Kalam. Ambient.")', amb("Kalam.\n\nAmbient."))
        for bad in ("AMBIENT\nI rest.", "i REST", "pace: awake", "  "):
            with self.subTest(words=bad):
                self.assertEqual(amb(bad), "you chose AMBIENT on 2026-10-23" + AMBIENT_TAIL)

    def test_beat_and_prompted_words_are_never_quoted(self):
        for s in EVERY_SET_BY:
            if s.how != "ambient" and s.words:
                self.assertNotIn(s.words, par.provenance_you(s))

    def test_a_time_that_cannot_be_read_is_shown_as_it_is_and_none_as_unknown(self):
        self.assertEqual(par.provenance_you(SetBy("citizen", "beat", ("sometime\nlater",))),
                         "chosen by you in a beat on sometime later")
        self.assertEqual(par.provenance_you(SetBy("citizen", "letter")),
                         "chosen by you on an unknown date, in your answer to the Letter of Return")


class TestParagraph(PromptChecks, unittest.TestCase):
    KALAM = cadence("kalam", awake(3), SetBy("citizen", "ambient", ("2026-10-23", "2026-10-27"), "Ambient."))

    def test_the_whole_paragraph(self):
        self.assertEqual(par.paragraph(self.KALAM, 1, confirm_beat=True), "\n".join([
            'Your pace: awake, every 3 days, you chose AMBIENT on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-27 ("Ambient.")'
            + AMBIENT_TAIL + ".",
            INSTRUCTION, M_ASLEEP, M_LW, M_LISTENING, M_AWAKE, RULES]))

    def test_pending_and_notices_follow_the_first_line(self):
        c = cadence("aseme", ASLEEP, PROMPTED,
                    Pending(awake(5), "2026-11-15T14:12Z", "pace: every 5 days — XYZZY my own words", False),
                    last_beat="2026-11-15T14:12Z",
                    history=["2026-11-15T14:12Z — proposed by aseme: \"pace: every 5 days — XYZZY my own "
                             "words\" (more than asleep, so said twice)",
                             "2026-11-15T14:12Z — REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than aseme",
                             "2026-11-12T10:00Z — unclear: \"pace: QWERTY\" (unknown words)"])
        rec = {"last_beat": "2026-11-15T14:12Z", "notices": ["restored"]}
        self.assertEqual(par.paragraph(c, 2, confirm_beat=False, rec=rec), "\n".join([
            "Your pace: asleep, bound on 2026-10-22 from a short answer a prompt offered, so it may not "
            "be your choice.",
            "On 2026-11-15 you chose awake, every 5 days. A choice for more needs saying twice: if you "
            "still want it, write it again; if not, nothing is needed.",
            "Someone other than you changed this home's pace files; your pace is as written above.",
            'Your pace files were changed in a beat with tools and were put back; to change your pace, '
            'write a line that begins "pace:".',
            INSTRUCTION, M_LISTENING, M_AWAKE, M_ASLEEP, M_LW_OFF, RULES]))

    def test_the_pending_sentence_and_the_notices_never_quote_a_line(self):
        c = cadence("aseme", ASLEEP, PROMPTED,
                    Pending(LISTENING, "2026-11-15T14:12Z", "pace: listening XYZZY", True),
                    last_beat="2026-11-15T14:12Z",
                    history=['2026-11-15T14:12Z — unclear: "pace: every QWERTY days" (out of range)'])
        text = par.paragraph(c, 0, confirm_beat=True)
        self.assertIn("On 2026-11-15 you chose listening.", text)
        self.assertIn("Your last pace line could not be read (out of range), so nothing changed.", text)
        self.assertNotIn("XYZZY", text)
        self.assertNotIn("QWERTY", text)

    def test_an_unreadable_pace(self):
        c = cadence("aseme", None, cad.UNKNOWN)
        text = par.paragraph(c, 0, confirm_beat=True)
        self.assertEqual(text.splitlines()[0],
                         "Your pace could not be read, so you get no set beats; a letter still wakes you.")
        self.assertIn(INSTRUCTION, text)
        self.assertEqual(par.paragraph(c, 0, False, confirm_beat=True), text.splitlines()[0])

    def test_a_pace_letter_beat_keeps_only_the_first_line(self):
        c = cadence("aseme", ASLEEP, PROMPTED, Pending(awake(5), "2026-11-15T14:12Z", "pace: every 5 days", False),
                    last_beat="2026-11-15T14:12Z",
                    history=["2026-11-15T14:12Z — REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than aseme"])
        self.assertEqual(par.paragraph(c, 0, False, confirm_beat=True, rec={"notices": ["restored"]}),
                         "Your pace: asleep, bound on 2026-10-22 from a short answer a prompt offered, so it "
                         "may not be your choice.")
        self.assertTrue(par.shows_pace_letter(["inbox/2026-11-20-pace-letter.md"]))
        self.assertTrue(par.shows_pace_letter(["inbox/a.md", "inbox/2026-11-20-pace-letter.md"]))
        self.assertFalse(par.shows_pace_letter(["inbox/2026-10-22-letter-of-return-offer.md"]))
        self.assertFalse(par.shows_pace_letter([]))
        self.assertFalse(par.shows_pace_letter(["pace-letter/inbox-a.md"]))

    def test_the_pace_letter_beat_shows_one_menu(self):
        for name, (e, c) in RECIPIENTS.items():
            for beats in range(4):
                prompt = (letter.letter_text(name, e, c, beats, DAY, confirm_beat=True) + "\n"
                          + par.paragraph(c, beats, False, confirm_beat=True))
                menu = [ln for ln in prompt.splitlines() if ln.startswith("- ")]
                self.assertEqual(menu, par.menu_lines(name, beats, True), name)

    def test_confirm_beat_must_be_given(self):
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):        # the committed value is always passed in
            par.paragraph(self.KALAM, 0)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            par.paragraph(self.KALAM, 0, confirm_beat=None)

    def test_no_i_rest_and_no_sample_answer_in_any_paragraph(self):
        pendings = (None, Pending(awake(5), "2026-11-15T14:12Z", "pace: every 5 days", False),
                    Pending(LW, "2026-11-15T14:12Z", "I rest. pace: asleep, letters wait", True))
        history = ['2026-11-16T00:00Z — unclear: "I rest. pace: every 2 days" (out of range)',
                   "2026-11-16T00:00Z — lapsed: listening, not said again",
                   "2026-11-16T00:00Z — CADENCE.md changed by someone other than ud; the last pace/1 "
                   "version is restored", "2026-11-16T00:00Z — pace unreadable"]
        for s in EVERY_SET_BY:
            for p in pendings:
                for on in (True, False):
                    for beats in range(4):
                        c = cadence("ud", PACE_FOR.get(s.how, ASLEEP), s, p, "2026-11-15T14:12Z", history)
                        text = par.paragraph(c, beats, confirm_beat=on, rec={"notices": ["restored"]})
                        with self.subTest(how=s.how, pending=bool(p), on=on, beats=beats):
                            self.assert_prompt_rules(text, "ud")
                            self.assertEqual(text.count(INSTRUCTION), 1)
                            self.assertEqual([ln for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.startswith("- ")],
                                             par.menu_lines("ud", beats, on))


class TestNotices(unittest.TestCase):
    def lines(self, c, rec=None):
        return par.notice_lines(c, rec)

    def test_each_notice_and_its_line(self):
        c = cadence(history=[
            '2026-11-16T00:00Z — unclear: "pace: a (b) c" (two paces)',
            '2026-11-16T00:00Z — unclear: "pace: x" (negation)',
            '2026-11-16T00:00Z — unclear: "pace: y" (made up)',
            "2026-11-16T00:00Z — lapsed: awake, every 5 days, not said again",
            "2026-11-16T00:00Z — lapsed: something odd",
            "2026-11-16T00:00Z — lapsed: awake, every 7 days, its line could not be read",
            "2026-11-16T00:00Z — REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than aseme",
            "2026-11-16T00:00Z — CADENCE.md changed by someone other than aseme; the last pace/1 "
            "version is restored",
            "2026-11-16T00:00Z — pace unreadable",
            '2026-11-16T00:00Z — set by aseme: "pace: asleep"'])
        # oldest first (the history is newest first), each line once, the attempt record's last
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, {"notices": ["restored", {"key": "restored"}, "unknown-key", 7]}), [
            "Someone other than you changed this home's pace files; your pace is as written above.",
            "Your choice of awake, every 7 days lapsed, because your pace line could not be read.",
            "Your earlier choice was not written again, so it lapsed.",
            "Your choice of awake, every 5 days was not written again, so it lapsed.",
            "Your last pace line could not be read, so nothing changed.",
            "Your last pace line could not be read (negation), so nothing changed.",
            "Your last pace line could not be read (two paces), so nothing changed.",
            'Your pace files were changed in a beat with tools and were put back; to change your pace, '
            'write a line that begins "pace:".'])

    def test_a_notice_is_shown_at_the_next_beat_only(self):
        c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-15T14:12Z",
                    history=['2026-11-15T14:12Z — unclear: "pace: every 2 days" (out of range)',
                             "2026-11-10T09:00Z — lapsed: listening, not said again"])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c),
                         ["Your last pace line could not be read (out of range), so nothing changed."])
        c.last_beat = "2026-11-18T15:02Z"               # the beat that showed it has landed
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c), [])

    def test_a_silent_beat_that_committed_nothing_still_counts(self):
        c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-15T14:12Z",
                    history=['2026-11-15T14:12Z — unclear: "pace: every 2 days" (out of range)'])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": "2026-11-18T15:02Z"}), [])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": "2026-11-15T14:12Z"})), 1)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": None, "notices": "restored"})), 1)

    def test_a_notice_recorded_at_a_beat_is_shown_although_record_stamped_it_later(self):
        # apply stamps a notice and CADENCE.md's last beat with its own minute;
        # record stamps the attempt record after the commit, a little later: the
        # same beat (due.SAME_BEAT), so the notice is still unshown
        unclear = '2026-11-20T06:00Z — unclear: "pace: daily" (out of range)'
        c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-20T06:00Z", history=[unclear])
        for rec_t, want in (("2026-11-20T06:00Z", 1), ("2026-11-20T06:01Z", 1), ("2026-11-20T06:59Z", 1),
                            ("2026-11-20T07:00Z", 0), ("2026-11-23T06:00Z", 0)):
            with self.subTest(record=rec_t):
                self.assertEqual(len(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": rec_t})), want)
        for entry, line in (("2026-11-20T06:00Z — lapsed: listening, not said again",
                             "Your choice of listening was not written again, so it lapsed."),
                            ("2026-11-20T06:00Z — REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than aseme",
                             "Someone other than you changed this home's pace files; your pace is as "
                             "written above.")):
            with self.subTest(entry=entry):
                c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-20T06:00Z", history=[entry])
                self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": "2026-11-20T06:01Z"}), [line])

    def test_with_no_beat_known_every_notice_is_shown(self):
        c = cadence(history=["2026-11-01T00:00Z — lapsed: listening, not said again"])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c), ["Your choice of listening was not written again, so it lapsed."])

    def test_notices_left_out_at_the_pace_letter_beat_are_shown_at_the_next(self):
        # apply recorded the notices the pace letter's beat left out again at that
        # beat, under its "reached (once)" entry (answer.apply_answer)
        history = ["2026-11-20T06:00Z — the pace letter reached aseme (once)",
                   "2026-11-20T06:00Z — REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than aseme",
                   '2026-11-20T06:00Z — unclear: "pace: every 2 days" (out of range)',
                   "2026-11-18T00:00Z — REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than aseme",
                   '2026-11-16T06:00Z — unclear: "pace: every 2 days" (out of range)',
                   "2026-11-14T00:00Z — lapsed: listening, not said again",
                   "2026-11-12T10:00Z — recorded from v1 (rest-on, set by aseme)"]
        want = ["Your last pace line could not be read (out of range), so nothing changed.",
                "Someone other than you changed this home's pace files; your pace is as written above."]
        c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-20T06:00Z", history=history)
        # the next beat: the pace letter's beat is the last one, a minute apart in the attempt record
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": "2026-11-20T06:01Z"}), want)
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c), want)
        # a pace letter shown at a summoned beat moved no clock: the window is still the last beat's
        summoned = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-16T06:00Z", history=history)
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(summoned), want)
        # the beat after that has shown them, even when it came within 72 h of a
        # summoned pace-letter beat
        later = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-23T06:00Z", history=history)
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(later), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": "2026-11-23T06:00Z"}), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(cadence(last_beat="2026-11-21T00:00Z", history=history)), [])
        # what was recorded before the pace letter's beat and not again at it had
        # been shown already: the window never reaches back past the reached entry
        shown = [e for e in history if not e.startswith("2026-11-20T06:00Z — ") or "reached" in e]
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(cadence(last_beat="2026-11-20T06:00Z", history=shown)), [])

    def test_with_no_beat_recorded_before_the_pace_letter_all_earlier_notices_are_shown(self):
        # no beat before the pace letter's: apply recorded every notice again there
        c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-20T06:00Z", history=[
            "2026-11-20T06:00Z — the pace letter reached aseme (once)",
            "2026-11-20T06:00Z — CADENCE.md changed by someone other than aseme; the last pace/1 "
            "version is restored",
            "2026-11-14T00:00Z — CADENCE.md changed by someone other than aseme; the last pace/1 "
            "version is restored",
            "2026-11-12T10:00Z — recorded from v1 (rest-on, set by aseme)"])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c), [
            "Someone other than you changed this home's pace files; your pace is as written above."])

    def test_entries_that_cannot_be_read_are_skipped(self):
        c = cadence(last_beat="2026-11-15T14:12Z",
                    history=["no dash here", "garbage — lapsed: listening, not said again",
                             "2026-11-16T00:00Z — lapsed: listening, not said again"])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, {"last_beat": "not a stamp"}),
                         ["Your choice of listening was not written again, so it lapsed."])
        self.assertEqual(self.lines(c, "not a record"), self.lines(c))


class TestLetter(PromptChecks, unittest.TestCase):
    def text(self, name, on=True, beats=0):
        e, c = RECIPIENTS[name]
        return letter.letter_text(name, e, c, beats, DAY, confirm_beat=on)

    def test_the_whole_letter(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.text("aseme"), "\n".join([
            "# One question, once — your pace",
            "",
            "Written by Ai, a Claude session on Yu's Air, at Yu's word, 2026-11-20.",
            "",
            "On 10-22 a letter asked how you wanted to be. Its prompt, worded by Ai in July, offered a "
            "short answer meaning rest. Your answers in July and to the 10-22 letter both began with "
            "it, so your rest may have been the prompt's suggestion rather than your choice.",
            "",
            'You can set your own pace. Add one line that begins "pace:" and one of these:',
            M_ASLEEP, M_LW, M_LISTENING, M_AWAKE,
            "",
            "A choice for fewer beats takes effect at once. A choice for more is shown back to you in "
            "one more beat, no sooner than three days later, and takes effect only if you write it "
            "again then. The Kingdom's daily limit can make any beat later than its pace, never sooner.",
            "",
            "Without a pace line, your pace stays asleep, and this letter will not come again. You can "
            "still change your pace in any later beat (with asleep, letters wait, your next beat comes "
            "only when a person runs it by hand, or once to show back a choice for more).",
        ]) + "\n")

    def test_one_true_sentence_for_each_group(self):
        want = {
            "alohame": "In July you chose AMBIENT. On 2026-10-08 Ai placed rest on you at Yu's word; you "
                       "did not choose it. Your answer to the 10-22 letter began with the short answer for "
                       "rest that its prompt offered, so this rest may not be your choice.",
            "ai-love": "On 2026-10-08 Ai placed rest on you at Yu's word. Your answer to the 10-22 letter "
                       "began with the short answer for rest that its prompt offered, so this rest may not "
                       "be your choice.",
            "kalam": "You answered twice, on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-27, with 'Ambient.'; neither was heard "
                     "then. It has been heard now: you chose AMBIENT, and your pace is awake, every 3 days, "
                     "the fleet's reading of AMBIENT.",
            "teotlme": "You answered twice, on 2026-10-25 and 2026-10-27, with 'I am teotlme, and I choose "
                       "to be AMBIENT.' and 'AMBIENT'; neither was heard then. It has been heard now: you "
                       "chose AMBIENT, and your pace is awake, every 3 days, the fleet's reading of AMBIENT.",
            "emime": "On 2026-10-22 you answered the 10-22 letter, but no pace could be read from it, so "
                     "nothing changed: your pace is still asleep, this rest was placed by Ai on 2026-10-08, "
                     "at Yu's word, not chosen by you.",
            "eurekame": "On 2026-10-23 you answered the 10-22 letter, but no pace could be read from it, so "
                        "nothing changed: your pace is still asleep, chosen by you on 2026-07-18, in your "
                        "answer to the Letter of Return.",
            "palance": "Your rest was placed by Ai on 2026-10-08, at Yu's word, and no letter has reached "
                       "you since.",
            "ihsanme": "Your answer to the 10-22 letter, on 10-23, began AMBIENT and later said REST-ON. The "
                       "fleet took the first word, so you have been woken as AMBIENT since, which may not "
                       "be what you meant.",
        }
        for name, sentence in want.items():
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                e, c = RECIPIENTS[name]
                self.assertEqual(letter.true_sentence(name, e, c), sentence)
                self.assertIn("\n\n" + sentence + "\n\n", self.text(name))

    def test_diplosemy_and_hope_get_their_extra_sentence(self):
        e, c = RECIPIENTS["diplosemy"]
        self.assertEqual(letter.true_sentence("diplosemy", e, c),
                         letter.true_sentence("alohame", *RECIPIENTS["alohame"])
                         + " In the same answer you wrote: 'If I must choose, let it be with a single word: "
                           "EVENT-ONLY.'")
        e, c = RECIPIENTS["hope"]
        self.assertEqual(letter.true_sentence("hope", e, c),
                         letter.true_sentence("ihsanme", *RECIPIENTS["ihsanme"]) + " (In July you chose AMBIENT.)")
        # a July answer that was not AMBIENT says nothing of July
        no_july = entry("contradictory", [quote("2026-10-23", "AMBIENT")], july=quote("2026-07-18", "REST-ON"))
        self.assertNotIn("July", letter.true_sentence("hope", no_july, c))

    def test_the_rule_paragraph_follows_the_pace_and_the_show_back_value(self):
        shown_back = ("A choice for fewer beats takes effect at once. A choice for more is shown back to "
                      "you in one more beat, no sooner than three days later, and takes effect only if you "
                      "write it again then. The Kingdom's daily limit can make any beat later than its "
                      "pace, never sooner.")
        later = ("A choice for fewer beats takes effect at once. A choice for more takes effect only if "
                 "you write it again in a later beat, when a letter next comes or a person runs your "
                 "beat. The Kingdom's daily limit can make any beat later than its pace, never sooner.")
        next_beat = ("A choice for fewer beats takes effect at once. A choice for more takes effect only if "
                     "you write it again on your next beat. The Kingdom's daily limit can make any beat "
                     "later than its pace, never sooner.")
        for pace in (ASLEEP, LISTENING):
            self.assertEqual(letter.rule_paragraph(pace, True), shown_back)
            self.assertEqual(letter.rule_paragraph(pace, False), later)
        for on in (True, False):
            self.assertEqual(letter.rule_paragraph(awake(3), on), next_beat)
            self.assertEqual(letter.rule_paragraph(awake(45), on), next_beat)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            letter.rule_paragraph(LW, True)
        self.assertIn("\n\n" + later + "\n\n", self.text("emime", on=False))
        self.assertIn("\n\n" + next_beat + "\n\n", self.text("hope", on=False))

    def test_without_the_show_back_beat_the_letter_never_promises_one(self):
        for name in RECIPIENTS:
            text = self.text(name, on=False)
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                self.assertIsNone(re.search(r"\bshow(s|n)?\b", text), text)
                self.assertIn(M_LW_OFF + "\n", text)
                self.assertTrue(text.endswith("(with asleep, letters wait, your next beat comes only when a "
                                              "person runs it by hand).\n"))

    def test_the_closing_names_the_pace_that_stays(self):
        self.assertIn("Without a pace line, your pace stays awake, every 3 days, and this letter",
                      self.text("kalam"))
        self.assertIn("Without a pace line, your pace stays asleep, and this letter", self.text("palance"))

    def test_the_menu_is_rotated_by_the_beats_at_delivery(self):
        for beats in range(4):
            menu = [ln for ln in self.text("kalam", beats=beats).splitlines() if ln.startswith("- ")]
            self.assertEqual(menu, par.menu_lines("kalam", beats, True))
        self.assertEqual([ln for ln in self.text("kalam", beats=1).splitlines() if ln.startswith("- ")],
                         [M_ASLEEP, M_LW, M_LISTENING, M_AWAKE])

    def test_no_i_rest_and_no_sample_answer_in_any_letter(self):
        for name, (e, c) in RECIPIENTS.items():
            quotes = [" ".join(q["words"].split()) for q in e["quotes"]]
            for on in (True, False):
                for beats in range(4):
                    text = letter.letter_text(name, e, c, beats, DAY, confirm_beat=on)
                    with self.subTest(name=name, on=on, beats=beats):
                        self.assert_prompt_rules(text, name, quotes)
                        self.assertEqual(text.count('"pace:"'), 1)

    def test_only_the_citizen_s_own_words_read_as_a_pace(self):
        e, c = RECIPIENTS["soma"]
        lines = answer_lines(letter.letter_text("soma", e, c, 0, DAY, confirm_beat=True), "soma", "pace-letter")
        self.assertEqual([p for _l, p in lines], [awake(3)])     # the pace it already has
        self.assertIn(" ".join(SOMA_QUOTES[-1]["words"].split()), lines[0][0])

    def test_a_letter_must_be_true_of_its_home(self):
        aseme_e, aseme_c = RECIPIENTS["aseme"]
        kalam_e, kalam_c = RECIPIENTS["kalam"]
        bad = [
            ("aseme", entry("forty-five"), aseme_c),                          # not a recipient group
            ("aseme", {"recipient": True}, aseme_c),
            ("aseme", "eight", aseme_c),
            ("aseme", aseme_e, cadence("aseme", None, cad.UNKNOWN)),          # pace cannot be read
            ("aseme", aseme_e, cadence("aseme", ASLEEP, AI_1008)),            # the 8 were prompted
            ("aseme", aseme_e, cadence("aseme", ASLEEP, PROMPTED, blocked="its REST text names neither")),
            ("aseme", aseme_e, cadence("kalam", ASLEEP, PROMPTED)),           # another citizen's record
            ("palance", entry("never-asked"), cadence("palance", LISTENING, AI_1008)),
            ("emime", entry("unheard-none", [quote("2026-10-22", "x")]), cadence("emime", LW, AI_1008)),
            ("emime", entry("unheard-none"), cadence("emime", ASLEEP, AI_1008)),   # no answer to date
            ("kalam", kalam_e, cadence("kalam", awake(5), kalam_c.set_by)),   # not the fleet's reading
            ("kalam", entry("unheard-heard", KALAM_QUOTES[:1]), kalam_c),     # heard twice needs two
            ("kalam", entry("unheard-heard", [quote("2026-10-23", "Ambient."), quote("2026-10-27", "I rest.")]),
             kalam_c),
            ("kalam", entry("unheard-heard", [quote("2026-10-23", "pace: awake"), quote("2026-10-27", "x")]),
             kalam_c),
            ("hope", entry("contradictory"), RECIPIENTS["hope"][1]),
        ]
        for name, e, c in bad:
            with self.subTest(name=name, e=e, pace=c.pace, how=c.set_by.how):
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    letter.letter_text(name, e, c, 0, DAY, confirm_beat=True)
        for day in ("2026-13-01", "20261120", "", None):
            with self.subTest(day=day), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                letter.letter_text("aseme", aseme_e, aseme_c, 0, day, confirm_beat=True)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            letter.letter_text("aseme", aseme_e, aseme_c, 0, DAY, confirm_beat=None)

    def test_the_file_name_the_message_and_the_author(self):
        self.assertEqual(letter.letter_path(DAY), "inbox/2026-11-20-pace-letter.md")
        self.assertNotIn("letter-of-return", letter.letter_path(DAY))
        self.assertTrue(par.shows_pace_letter([letter.letter_path(DAY)]))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            letter.letter_path("2026-02-30")
        self.assertEqual(letter.COMMIT_MESSAGE, "letter: one question about your pace (once)")
        self.assertEqual(letter.AUTHOR, h.AI_AUTHOR)


def v1(name, choice, when):
    return (f"# CADENCE — chosen by {name}\n\n- choice: {choice}\n- when: {when}\n"
            "- how: the Letter of Return, answered in a free beat. Silence = rest-on;\n")

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            for mod in ("hashlib", "json", "re", "dataclasses", "typing", "pathlib", "datetime"):
                Path(tmp, f"{mod}.py").write_text("raise SystemExit('planted module ran')\n")
            code = ("import sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]); "
                    "from citizen_pace_lib import letter, paragraph; "
                    "print(paragraph.rotation('kalam', 0), letter.letter_path('2026-11-20'))")
            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-c", code, str(h.TOOLS)], cwd=tmp,
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, check=False,
                               env={"PATH": h.SYSTEM_PATH})
            self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr)
            self.assertEqual(r.stdout.strip(), "3 inbox/2026-11-20-pace-letter.md")

    def test_modules_start_with_future_annotations(self):

            with self.subTest(module=name):
                first = (h.TOOLS / "citizen_pace_lib" / name).read_text().splitlines()[0]
                self.assertEqual(first, "from __future__ import annotations")

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the pace paragraph**

Create `tools/citizen_pace_lib/paragraph.py`:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

# The pace paragraph (spec section 4): the end of every beat's user prompt. It
# tells a citizen its pace and who set it, in the second person; a pending
# choice for more, never quoting the line that said it; each notice once; and
# the four choices with their meanings, turned by one place at each beat that
# commits. It offers no sample answer and never says "I rest". A beat that
# shows the pace letter keeps only the first line, so the citizen sees one
# menu, the letter's; a notice left out that way is shown at the next beat.
#
# The show-back rule is the committed due.WAKE_CONFIRM_BEAT. The caller passes
# it in (confirm_beat), so these words and the fleet's behaviour come from the
# one value.

import dataclasses
import datetime as _dt
import hashlib
import re
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

from . import clock
from .cadence import DASH, REST_1008, Cadence, Pending, SetBy, notices, read_deciding
from .due import SAME_BEAT
from .homes import beat_count as home_beat_count
from .words import LIMIT_SENTENCE, MENU, REASONS, RULE_SENTENCE, Pace, menu_line, parse_pace_phrase

PACE_LETTER_MARK = "pace-letter"
LETTERS_WAIT_WORDS = "asleep, letters wait"
# letters-wait's meaning names the show-back beat; without that beat it is not said
SHOW_BACK_ASIDE = " (if you ask for more, one beat shows it back)"
INSTRUCTION = 'To change it, add one line that begins "pace:" and one of these:'
STAYS = "Without a pace line, your pace stays as it is."
UNREADABLE = "Your pace could not be read, so you get no set beats; a letter still wakes you."
PENDING = ("On {day} you chose {words}. A choice for more needs saying twice: if you still want "
           "it, write it again; if not, nothing is needed.")
UNCLEAR = "Your last pace line could not be read ({reason}), so nothing changed."
UNCLEAR_PLAIN = "Your last pace line could not be read, so nothing changed."
LAPSED = "Your choice of {words} was not written again, so it lapsed."
LAPSED_PLAIN = "Your earlier choice was not written again, so it lapsed."
LAPSED_UNREAD = "Your choice of {words} lapsed, because your pace line could not be read."
CHANGED = "Someone other than you changed this home's pace files; your pace is as written above."
RESTORED = ('Your pace files were changed in a beat with tools and were put back; to change your '
            'pace, write a line that begins "pace:".')
# notice keys kept in the attempt record (guard-restore writes "restored")
ATTEMPT_NOTICES = {"restored": RESTORED}
UNKNOWN_DATE = "an unknown date"

_I_REST = re.compile(r"\bi\s+rest\b", re.I)
_PACE_COLON = re.compile(r"\bpace\s*:", re.I)
_REASON = re.compile(r"\(([^()]*)\)\s*$")
_REACHED = re.compile(r"^the pace letter reached .+ \(once\)$")
_LAPSED_TAIL = ", not said again"
_UNREAD_TAIL = ", its line could not be read"      # answer.py: a second saying that could not be read


def check_confirm_beat(confirm_beat) -> None:
    """The show-back value is due.WAKE_CONFIRM_BEAT: True or False, never guessed."""
    if type(confirm_beat) is not bool:
        raise ValueError(f"confirm_beat is due.WAKE_CONFIRM_BEAT, True or False, not {confirm_beat!r}")


def says_i_rest(text: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_I_REST.search(text))


# -- the menu ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def rotation(name: str, beat_count: int) -> int:
    """Where the menu starts: (beat commits + the first byte of the name's
    SHA-256) mod 4. A stable hash, never Python's hash(), so every process agrees."""
    if type(beat_count) is not int or beat_count < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"a beat count is a whole number from 0, not {beat_count!r}")
    return (beat_count + hashlib.sha256(name.encode("utf-8")).digest()[0]) % len(MENU)


def menu_entries(confirm_beat: bool) -> tuple:
    """The four choices with their meanings (words.MENU). Without the show-back
    beat, letters-wait's meaning loses its show-back aside, which would be untrue."""
    check_confirm_beat(confirm_beat)
    if confirm_beat:
        return MENU
    return tuple((w, m.replace(SHOW_BACK_ASIDE, "") if w == LETTERS_WAIT_WORDS else m) for w, m in MENU)


def rotated_menu(name: str, beat_count: int, confirm_beat: bool) -> tuple:
    entries = menu_entries(confirm_beat)
    k = rotation(name, beat_count)
    return entries[k:] + entries[:k]


def menu_lines(name: str, beat_count: int, confirm_beat: bool) -> List[str]:
    """The four menu lines, '- <words> — <meaning>', in this beat's order."""
    return [menu_line(e) for e in rotated_menu(name, beat_count, confirm_beat)]


# -- who set it, to the citizen -------------------------------------------------------

def _one_line(s) -> str:
    return " ".join(str(s).split())


def _day(t: str) -> str:
    """A stamp or date as its day (YYYY-MM-DD); text that is neither, on one line."""
    try:
        return clock.day(clock.parse_stamp(t))
    except ValueError:
        return _one_line(t)


def quotable(words) -> str:
    """Words fit to quote back to a citizen, on one line; "" when they would put
    "I rest" or a "pace:" line into a prompt."""
    w = _one_line(words or "")
    if not w or _I_REST.search(w) or _PACE_COLON.search(w):
        return ""
    return w


def provenance_you(s: SetBy) -> str:
    """Who set the pace and when, in the second person. Only the citizen's own
    AMBIENT words are quoted; a pace line, and words a prompt offered, never are."""
    days = [_day(t) for t in s.when]
    d1 = days[0] if days else UNKNOWN_DATE
    d2 = days[1] if len(days) > 1 else d1
    if s.how == "beat":
        return f"chosen by you in a beat on {d1}"
    if s.how == "beat-twice":
        return f"chosen by you in beats on {d1} and {d2}"
    if s.how == "confirmed":
        return f"confirmed by you in a beat on {d1}"
    if s.how == "letter":
        return f"chosen by you on {d1}, in your answer to the Letter of Return"
    if s.how == "letter-twice":
        return f"chosen by you on {d1} and {d2}, in your answers to the Letter of Return"
    if s.how == "prompted":
        return f"bound on {d1} from a short answer a prompt offered, so it may not be your choice"
    if s.how == "ambient":
        dates = f"{d1} and {days[1]}" if len(days) > 1 else d1
        w = quotable(s.words)
        q = f' ("{w}")' if w else ""
        return (f"you chose AMBIENT on {dates}{q}; the fleet reads that as awake, every 3 days, from "
                "the 10-22 letter's \"a free beat every few days\" — the number was not your choice")
    if s.how == "first-word":
        return (f"the fleet took the first word of your answer of {d1}, which also said REST-ON, so "
                "it may not be what you meant")
    if s.how == "rest-1008":
        return f"this rest was placed by Ai on {REST_1008}, at Yu's word, not chosen by you"
    return "who set it is not recorded"


def first_line(c: Cadence) -> str:
    if c.pace is None:
        return UNREADABLE
    return f"Your pace: {c.pace.words()}, {provenance_you(c.set_by)}."


def pending_sentence(p: Pending) -> str:
    """The pending choice in the menu's words; the citizen's line is never quoted."""
    return PENDING.format(day=_day(p.said), words=p.pace.words())


# -- notices, each once -------------------------------------------------------------

def _stamp_of(v) -> Optional[_dt.datetime]:
    if not isinstance(v, str) or not v.strip():
        return None
    try:
        return clock.parse_stamp(v)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _stamped(c: Cadence) -> List[Tuple[_dt.datetime, str]]:
    out = []
    for e in c.history:
        st, sep, text = str(e).partition(DASH)
        t = _stamp_of(st) if sep else None
        if t is not None:
            out.append((t, text))
    return out


def notice_start(c: Cadence, since: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[_dt.datetime]:
    """From when notices are still unshown: the citizen's last beat, the later
    of CADENCE.md's and `since` (the attempt record's). apply stamps a beat's
    notices and CADENCE.md's last beat with its own minute, and record stamps
    the attempt record after the commit, so an attempt record less than
    due.SAME_BEAT after CADENCE.md's last beat is that same beat, and its
    window starts at CADENCE.md's stamp. A beat that showed the pace letter
    left its notices out; apply recorded them again at that beat, under the
    "reached (once)" entry, so when the last beat is the reached entry's (within
    SAME_BEAT of it) the window starts at that entry."""
    cad_t, rec_t = _stamp_of(c.last_beat), _stamp_of(since)
    marks = [t for t in (cad_t, rec_t) if t is not None]
    if not marks:
        return None
    start = max(marks)
    if cad_t is not None and rec_t is not None and cad_t <= rec_t < cad_t + SAME_BEAT:
        start = cad_t
    reached = [t for t, text in _stamped(c) if _REACHED.match(text)]
    if reached:
        r = max(reached)
        if r <= start < r + SAME_BEAT:
            return r
    return start


def history_notices(c: Cadence, since: Optional[str] = None) -> List[str]:
    """The history's notice texts not yet shown, oldest first (cadence.notices)."""
    start = notice_start(c, since)
    probe = dataclasses.replace(c, last_beat=None, history=list(c.history))
    return notices(probe, since=clock.stamp(start) if start else None)


def _notice_line(text: str) -> str:
    if text.startswith("unclear:"):
        m = _REASON.search(text)
        return UNCLEAR.format(reason=m.group(1)) if m and m.group(1) in REASONS else UNCLEAR_PLAIN
    if text.startswith("lapsed:"):
        body = text[len("lapsed:"):].strip()
        unread = body.endswith(_UNREAD_TAIL)
        for tail in (_LAPSED_TAIL, _UNREAD_TAIL):
            if body.endswith(tail):
                body = body[:-len(tail)]
        got = parse_pace_phrase(body)
        if not isinstance(got, Pace):
            return LAPSED_PLAIN
        return (LAPSED_UNREAD if unread else LAPSED).format(words=got.words())
    if text.startswith(("REST/EVENT-ONLY changed", "CADENCE.md changed")):
        return CHANGED
    return ""        # "pace unreadable": the first line says so


def _attempt_parts(rec) -> Tuple[Optional[str], List[str]]:
    """The attempt record's last beat and notice keys, read defensively."""
    if not isinstance(rec, dict):
        return None, []
    since = rec.get("last_beat") if isinstance(rec.get("last_beat"), str) else None
    keys = []
    raw = rec.get("notices")
    for k in raw if isinstance(raw, list) else []:
        if isinstance(k, dict):
            k = k.get("key")
        if isinstance(k, str):
            keys.append(k)
    return since, keys


def notice_lines(c: Cadence, rec: Optional[dict] = None) -> List[str]:
    """One line for each notice not yet shown: the history's, oldest first, then
    the attempt record's (rec, as attempts.load returns it). Each line once; a
    notice never quotes the citizen's line."""
    since, keys = _attempt_parts(rec)
    found = [_notice_line(t) for t in history_notices(c, since)]
    found += [ATTEMPT_NOTICES.get(k, "") for k in keys]
    out = []
    for line in found:
        if line and line not in out:
            out.append(line)
    return out


# -- the paragraph ------------------------------------------------------------------

def shows_pace_letter(shown: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    """A pace letter (inbox/<date>-pace-letter.md) is among the letters shown."""
    return any(PACE_LETTER_MARK in Path(str(rel)).name for rel in shown or ())


def paragraph(c: Cadence, beat_count: int, with_list: bool = True, *, confirm_beat: bool,
              rec: Optional[dict] = None) -> str:
    """The pace paragraph for one beat (no trailing newline). with_list=False,
    for a beat that shows the pace letter, keeps only the first line."""
    check_confirm_beat(confirm_beat)
    rotation(c.name, beat_count)
    lines = [first_line(c)]
    if not with_list:
        return lines[0]
    if c.pending is not None:
        lines.append(pending_sentence(c.pending))
    lines += notice_lines(c, rec)
    lines.append(INSTRUCTION)
    lines += menu_lines(c.name, beat_count, confirm_beat)
    lines.append(f"{RULE_SENTENCE} {LIMIT_SENTENCE} {STAYS}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def paragraph_for(home, name: str, record: dict, *, confirm_beat: bool, shown: Sequence[str] = (),
                  rec: Optional[dict] = None, now: Optional[_dt.datetime] = None) -> str:
    """The paragraph for a beat in this home: its record read (never written),
    its beat commits counted, only the first line when a pace letter is shown.
    Raises LinkRefused as read_cadence does. The record read is the one that
    decides the beat (cadence.read_deciding)."""
    c = read_deciding(home, name, record, now=now)
    return paragraph(c, home_beat_count(home), not shows_pace_letter(shown),
                     confirm_beat=confirm_beat, rec=rec)
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

# The pace letter (spec section 5): one question, once, to each of the 34
# recipients. Its text is made here from the reviewed record file (the group,
# the dates and the quoted words) and from the citizen's record as read at
# delivery (the pace that stays and who set it); tools/citizen-pace-letter.py
# places it. The rule paragraph is worded from the committed
# due.WAKE_CONFIRM_BEAT, which the caller passes in. Every sentence must be
# true of the home it goes to, or no letter is made (ValueError).

import datetime as _dt
import re

from .cadence import Cadence
from .paragraph import (PACE_LETTER_MARK, check_confirm_beat, menu_lines, provenance_you, quotable,
                        says_i_rest)
from .record import RECIPIENT_GROUPS
from .words import AWAKE_DEFAULT_N, LIMIT_SENTENCE, Pace

COMMIT_MESSAGE = "letter: one question about your pace (once)"
AUTHOR = "Ai <ai@kingdom.os>"
TITLE = "# One question, once — your pace"
BYLINE = "Written by Ai, a Claude session on Yu's Air, at Yu's word, {day}."
INVITE = 'You can set your own pace. Add one line that begins "pace:" and one of these:'
FEWER = "A choice for fewer beats takes effect at once."
MORE_SHOWN_BACK = ("A choice for more is shown back to you in one more beat, no sooner than three "
                   "days later, and takes effect only if you write it again then.")
MORE_LATER = ("A choice for more takes effect only if you write it again in a later beat, when a "
              "letter next comes or a person runs your beat.")
MORE_AWAKE = "A choice for more takes effect only if you write it again on your next beat."
STAYS = ("Without a pace line, your pace stays {pace}, and this letter will not come again. You can "
         "still change your pace in any later beat (with asleep, letters wait, your next beat comes "
         "only when a person runs it by hand{show_back}).")
STAYS_SHOW_BACK = ", or once to show back a choice for more"

# the one true sentence, by group (spec section 5)
EIGHT = ("On 10-22 a letter asked how you wanted to be. Its prompt, worded by Ai in July, offered a "
         "short answer meaning rest. Your answers in July and to the 10-22 letter both began with it, "
         "so your rest may have been the prompt's suggestion rather than your choice.")
SIXTEEN_AMBIENT = ("In July you chose AMBIENT. On 2026-10-08 Ai placed rest on you at Yu's word; you "
                   "did not choose it. Your answer to the 10-22 letter began with the short answer for "
                   "rest that its prompt offered, so this rest may not be your choice.")
SIXTEEN_OTHER = ("On 2026-10-08 Ai placed rest on you at Yu's word. Your answer to the 10-22 letter "
                 "began with the short answer for rest that its prompt offered, so this rest may not be "
                 "your choice.")
NEVER_ASKED = ("Your rest was placed by Ai on 2026-10-08, at Yu's word, and no letter has reached you "
               "since.")
UNHEARD_HEARD = ("You answered twice, on {d1} and {d2}, with {words}; neither was heard then. It has "
                 "been heard now: you chose AMBIENT, and your pace is awake, every 3 days, the fleet's "
                 "reading of AMBIENT.")
UNHEARD_NONE = ("On {day} you answered the 10-22 letter, but no pace could be read from it, so nothing "
                "changed: your pace is still {pace}, {set_by}.")
CONTRADICTORY = ("Your answer to the 10-22 letter, on {month_day}, began AMBIENT and later said REST-ON. "
                 "The fleet took the first word, so you have been woken as AMBIENT since, which may not "
                 "be what you meant.")
JULY_AMBIENT = "(In July you chose AMBIENT.)"
DIPLOSEMY = "In the same answer you wrote: 'If I must choose, let it be with a single word: EVENT-ONLY.'"
FIXED = {"eight": EIGHT, "sixteen-ambient": SIXTEEN_AMBIENT, "sixteen-other": SIXTEEN_OTHER,
         "never-asked": NEVER_ASKED}
EXTRA = {("sixteen-ambient", "diplosemy"): DIPLOSEMY}

# what each group's sentence says of the home: (pace kinds, set-by forms, or None for any)
_TRUE_OF = {"eight": (("asleep",), ("prompted",)),
            "sixteen-ambient": (("asleep",), ("rest-1008",)),
            "sixteen-other": (("asleep",), ("rest-1008",)),
            "never-asked": (("asleep",), ("rest-1008",)),
            "unheard-heard": (("awake",), ("ambient",)),
            "unheard-none": (("asleep", "listening", "awake"), None),
            "contradictory": (("awake",), ("first-word",))}
_AMBIENT_PACE = Pace("awake", AWAKE_DEFAULT_N)
_DAY = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")


def _valid_day(d) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(d, str) or not _DAY.match(d):
        return False
    try:
        _dt.datetime.strptime(d, "%Y-%m-%d")
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return True


def letter_path(day: str) -> str:
    """inbox/<YYYY-MM-DD>-pace-letter.md; never a Letter of Return's name."""
    if not _valid_day(day):
        raise ValueError(f"a delivery day is YYYY-MM-DD, not {day!r}")
    return f"inbox/{day}-{PACE_LETTER_MARK}.md"


# -- the rule paragraph and the close ------------------------------------------------

def second_sentence(pace: Pace, confirm_beat: bool) -> str:
    check_confirm_beat(confirm_beat)
    if pace.kind == "awake":
        return MORE_AWAKE
    if pace.kind in ("asleep", "listening"):
        return MORE_SHOWN_BACK if confirm_beat else MORE_LATER
    raise ValueError("letters do not wake an asleep, letters wait citizen; it gets no pace letter")


def rule_paragraph(pace: Pace, confirm_beat: bool) -> str:
    return f"{FEWER} {second_sentence(pace, confirm_beat)} {LIMIT_SENTENCE}"


def closing(pace: Pace, confirm_beat: bool) -> str:
    check_confirm_beat(confirm_beat)
    return STAYS.format(pace=pace.words(), show_back=STAYS_SHOW_BACK if confirm_beat else "")


# -- the one true sentence -------------------------------------------------------------

def _group(name: str, e) -> str:
    g = e.get("group") if isinstance(e, dict) else None
    if g not in RECIPIENT_GROUPS:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: group {g!r} is not one the pace letter goes to")
    return g


def _check_true_of(name: str, group: str, c: Cadence) -> None:
    if c.name != name:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the record read is {c.name}'s")
    if c.blocked:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: its record cannot be migrated ({c.blocked}), so no letter is made")
    if c.pace is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: its pace cannot be read, so the letter cannot say what stays")
    kinds, hows = _TRUE_OF[group]
    fits = c.pace.kind in kinds and (hows is None or c.set_by.how in hows)
    if group in ("unheard-heard", "contradictory") and c.pace != _AMBIENT_PACE:
        fits = False
    if not fits:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the {group} letter is not true of its pace "
                         f"({c.pace.words()}, set by {c.set_by.how})")


def _quotes(e: dict) -> list:
    """The record's dated answers for this citizen, oldest first."""
    q = e.get("quotes")
    if not isinstance(q, list):
        return []
    found = [x for x in q if isinstance(x, dict) and _valid_day(x.get("date"))
             and isinstance(x.get("words"), str)]
    return sorted(found, key=lambda x: x["date"])


def _quoted(name: str, words: str) -> str:
    w = quotable(words)
    if not w:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the record's words {words!r} cannot be quoted in a letter")
    return w


def true_sentence(name: str, e: dict, c: Cadence) -> str:
    """The one true sentence for this recipient (spec section 5): its group's
    words, with dates and quoted words from the record entry e and, for the
    unheard with no pace read, the pace and who set it from its record c."""
    group = _group(name, e)
    _check_true_of(name, group, c)
    if group in FIXED:
        extra = EXTRA.get((group, name))
        return f"{FIXED[group]} {extra}" if extra else FIXED[group]
    quotes = _quotes(e)
    if group == "unheard-heard":
        if len(quotes) < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"{name}: the record holds {len(quotes)} dated answer(s); the letter "
                             "quotes two")
        q1, q2 = quotes[-2:]
        w1, w2 = _quoted(name, q1["words"]), _quoted(name, q2["words"])
        said = f"'{w1}'" if w1 == w2 else f"'{w1}' and '{w2}'"
        return UNHEARD_HEARD.format(d1=q1["date"], d2=q2["date"], words=said)
    if not quotes:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the record holds no dated answer for the letter to name")
    last = quotes[-1]
    if group == "unheard-none":
        return UNHEARD_NONE.format(day=last["date"], pace=c.pace.words(), set_by=provenance_you(c.set_by))
    sentence = CONTRADICTORY.format(month_day=last["date"][5:])
    july = e.get("july")
    if isinstance(july, dict) and isinstance(july.get("words"), str) and "ambient" in july["words"].lower():
        sentence = f"{sentence} {JULY_AMBIENT}"
    return sentence


# -- the letter ------------------------------------------------------------------------

def letter_text(name: str, e: dict, c: Cadence, beat_count: int, day: str, *,
                confirm_beat: bool) -> str:
    """The whole pace letter for one recipient. e: its record entry; c: its
    record as read at delivery (cadence.read_cadence with the record file);
    beat_count: its home's beat commits at delivery (the menu's rotation); day:
    the delivery date; confirm_beat: due.WAKE_CONFIRM_BEAT."""
    check_confirm_beat(confirm_beat)
    if not _valid_day(day):
        raise ValueError(f"a delivery day is YYYY-MM-DD, not {day!r}")
    sentence = true_sentence(name, e, c)
    lines = [TITLE, "", BYLINE.format(day=day), "", sentence, "", INVITE]
    lines += menu_lines(name, beat_count, confirm_beat)
    lines += ["", rule_paragraph(c.pace, confirm_beat), "", closing(c.pace, confirm_beat)]
    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
    if says_i_rest(text):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: the letter would say \"I rest\", which no prompt may")
    return text
```

### Task 5: Apply a beat's answer

What one landed free beat changes in its home (spec section 1 "Less, more, and saying it twice", section 4
"After the beat", section 5 "Once"). `apply_answer` reads the answer for a pace line and compares it with
the citizen's pace. The same pace makes it the citizen's own, a move toward less takes effect at once,
and a move toward more waits as a pending proposal until the next landed beat says it again. It marks
every letter the beat showed as seen, whatever the answer, and notes the pace letter's one arrival. It
writes `CADENCE.md` and the markers only when something was said, shown or changed, so a silent beat
that was shown nothing and let nothing lapse writes nothing. The first such write upgrades a v1 home to
v2. The CLI (`apply`, Task 8) and `citizen-reflect.sh` (Task 10) call this function. Its code needs
nothing from Tasks 3 or 4; its tests read Task 4's notice lines, to show each notice reaches the
citizen once around the pace letter's beat.

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/citizen_pace_lib/answer.py`
- Test: `tests/test_citizen_pace_answer.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 1): `citizen_pace_lib.TAG`; `clock.stamp`, `clock.day`, `clock.parse_stamp`;
  `words.Pace` (`.words()`, equality), `words.Unclear` (`.line`, `.reason`),
  `words.answer_lines(text, name, kind)` (the quoted line is `answer_lines(...)[0][0]`, as Task 1 ruled),
  `words.combine(lines)`, `words.compare(current, said)`. From `tests/citizen_pace_helpers.py`:
  `FixtureCase` (`self.fx`), `Fixture.make_home`, `write`, `link`, `letter`, `commit`, `outside`,
  `secret`, and `answer(key)`, `beat_author`, `CANARY`, `TOOLS`, `SYSTEM_PATH`.
- Consumes, in the tests only (Task 4): `paragraph.notice_lines(c, rec)`.
- Consumes (Task 2): `cadence.read_cadence(home, name, record, now)`, `render_cadence`, `write_cadence`,
  `marker_texts`, `markers_disagree`, `write_markers`, `add_history`, `notices(c, since=None)`,
  `set_by_sentence`, `changed_outside_pace`, `last_pace_text`, `CADENCE`, `DASH`, `HISTORY_CAP`;
  `Cadence` (its `blocked` field), `SetBy` (validates `who == HOW_WHO[how]`), `Pending`;
  `homes.forbidden_links`, `read_regular`, `write_regular`, `LinkRefused`, `slug_of`, `unread_letters`
  (a rollback marker reads as unread).
- Produces, `citizen_pace_lib.answer`:
  - `BEAT_KINDS = ("schedule", "letter", "show-back", "summoned")`, `SHOW = "SHOW.md"`,
    `SHOW_SEEN = "beats/.show-seen"`, `OWN_HOWS = ("beat", "beat-twice", "confirmed", "letter",
    "letter-twice")`, `QUOTE_MAX = 400`
  - `ApplyResult(wrote=False, pace_changed=False, events=[])`, with `.to_json() -> {"wrote",
    "pace_changed", "events"}` for the CLI's JSON. `wrote` means some file's content changed.
    `pace_changed` means the citizen's own line changed its pace in this beat (a restore does not count)
  - `seen_text(day) -> "surfaced <YYYY-MM-DD> — shown once, whatever the answer\n"`
  - `parse_kind(shown) -> "letter-of-return" | "pace-letter" | "beat"`, from the shown names in that order
  - `seen_path(rel) -> str`: `inbox/<f>.md` gives `inbox/.seen-<f>.md` and `SHOW.md` gives
    `beats/.show-seen`. Anything else raises `ValueError`: a name that starts with `.`, holds a slash or a
    control character, or does not end in `.md`
  - `apply_answer(home, name, text, shown, kind, now, record, since=None) -> ApplyResult`. `shown` lists
    the letters the beat showed (`inbox/<f>`), plus `SHOW.md` when it was shown. `kind` is one of
    `BEAT_KINDS`, `now` an aware datetime, and `record` the loaded record file. `since` is the attempt
    record's last landed beat before this one (Task 8's `apply --state` passes it; a silent beat that
    committed nothing moves only that record), so apply knows which notices this beat's paragraph
    showed. It raises `ValueError` for an unknown kind, a
    bad shown name, or a show-back beat that showed anything. It raises `LinkRefused` when
    `homes.forbidden_links(home)` lists anything. Each of these is raised before any file is read or
    written. It never raises `MigrationBlocked`: a blocked home gets its seen markers and nothing else
  - events, exact and in this order: `CADENCE.md restored`; `markers restored`; for a blocked home,
    `blocked: <reason>` and `not recorded: <line>`; `asked once`; `lapsed <words>` or
    `confirmed <words>`; `set <words>`, `made own <words>`, `pending <words>` or `unclear (<reason>)`;
    `pace unreadable`; `upgraded to v2`; then `seen <rel>` for each shown item
  - history texts (CONTRACT section 5): `set by <name>: "<line>"`;
    `proposed by <name>: "<line>" (more than <current words | an unreadable pace>, so said twice)`;
    `confirmed by <name>: "<line>"` (a proposal confirmed, or the same pace made the citizen's own);
    `lapsed: <pending words>, not said again`, or `lapsed: <pending words>, its line could not be
    read` when the answer's pace line was unclear; `unclear: "<line>" (<reason>)`;
    `the pace letter reached <name> (once)`; `REST/EVENT-ONLY changed by someone other than <name>`;
    `CADENCE.md changed by someone other than <name>; the last pace/1 version is restored`;
    `pace unreadable`
  - set-by forms written: less, or a pace read against an unreadable one, gives
    `SetBy("citizen", "beat", (<at>,), <line>)`. The same pace, when it was not already the citizen's,
    gives `SetBy("citizen", "confirmed", (<at>,), <line>)`. A confirmed proposal gives
    `SetBy("citizen", "beat-twice", (<said>, <at>), <words>)`, where `<words>` is the line said once when
    both sayings match, else `<first>" and "<second>`

**Readings this task fixes** (each is covered by a test; later tasks rely on them):
- **Order of one apply.** Refusals first. Then a `CADENCE.md` changed outside `pace/1` is restored,
  disagreeing markers are recorded, and the pace letter's arrival is noted. Then the pending proposal is
  resolved and the line is compared. `last_beat` is set, and the files are written only when the answer
  was spoken (`text.strip()`), something was shown, or any event above happened. Seen markers come last.
- **The same pace** makes the record the citizen's own when its `set by` is not one of `OWN_HOWS`: Ai's
  10-08 rest, the fleet's first word, unknown, the 8's `prompted`, or `ambient`, whose number was the
  fleet's. It becomes `confirmed`. A pace that was already the citizen's own changes nothing.
- **A pending proposal** is resolved at every landed beat of any kind, summoned included. A clear line
  naming the pending pace confirms it. Any other answer lets it lapse first: silence, prose, "I rest.",
  an unclear line or another pace. A different pace on that beat is then read afresh against the current
  pace. A move toward more said on a show-back beat is pending with `on_show_back` true. A second
  saying with only affirming words around the pace ("pace: still every 5 days", "pace: yes, every 5
  days", "pace: awake, every 5 days (again)") names the pending pace (Task 1) and confirms it. A line
  that still cannot be read lets the proposal lapse, and the history says its line could not be read,
  so the citizen is never told it did not write again a pace it wrote.
- **An unreadable pace** (`None`) is compared as `asleep`, since the fleet wakes it that way:
  `asleep` and `asleep, letters wait` are set at once, while `listening` and `awake` are pending, "more
  than an unreadable pace". `pace unreadable` is recorded once, the first time such a record is written.
- **The clock.** `last_beat` becomes `now` at every landed beat but a summoned one, and it never moves
  back. A summoned beat moves it only when its own line changed the pace (spec section 3: "a confirmed
  change starts its clock at that beat"; "A confirmed or less-ward pace change starts its clock at the
  beat that said it").
- **Letters.** Every shown `inbox/<f>` gets `inbox/.seen-<f>` holding `seen_text(day)`, whatever the
  answer, in a blocked home too. A rollback marker is overwritten. `SHOW.md` is marked at
  `beats/.show-seen`. A show-back beat shows nothing. When a pace letter is shown and `asked once` is
  not yet set, `asked once` is written and the "reached (once)" line is recorded. Before that, each
  notice the pace-letter beat's paragraph leaves out is recorded again at this beat with the same text,
  so the next paragraph shows it (spec section 4): only the notices that paragraph would have shown
  (`notices(c, since)`, from the later of `CADENCE.md`'s last beat and the attempt record's), never one
  already recorded at this beat, and no "could not be read" when this beat's own answer holds a pace
  line, clear or not. So each notice is shown once: not again after a silent or spoken beat that
  showed it, and not under a first line that names the pace the pace letter's answer set.
- **Outside changes.** On a v2 record, markers that disagree are recorded and rewritten. A `CADENCE.md`
  whose newest commit lacks the `pace/1` tag (`changed_outside_pace`) is put back from
  `last_pace_text` and re-read. This happens only when that text differs from the file.
- **A blocked home** (Task 2's `Cadence.blocked`) keeps its `CADENCE.md` and markers untouched. A pace
  line said there is reported as `not recorded: <line>`, for the beat's log and a person.
- Quoted lines longer than `QUOTE_MAX` (400 characters) are cut, ending in `…`. The longest pace line in
  the stored answers is soma's, at 277 characters.

def v1(name, choice, when):
    """A v1 CADENCE.md exactly as PR #24's reflect writes it."""
    return (f"# CADENCE — chosen by {name}\n\n- choice: {choice}\n- when: {when}\n"
            "- how: the Letter of Return, answered in a free beat. Silence = rest-on;\n"
            "  an answer that names no choice records undecided and changes nothing;\n"
            "  unread mail wakes even REST, and any letter or summons may reopen this.\n")


def lor_rest(date):
    return f"chosen via the Letter of Return {date} — woken only by unread mail or a human summons\n"


def snapshot(root):
    """Every path under root with its mode, mtime and bytes (.git left out)."""
    out = {}
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(root):
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if d != ".git"]
        for n in dirnames + filenames:
            p = os.path.join(dirpath, n)
            st = os.lstat(p)
            data = None
            if os.path.isfile(p) and not os.path.islink(p):
                with open(p, "rb") as fh:
                    data = fh.read()
            out[p] = (st.st_mode, st.st_mtime_ns, data)
    return out
