```python
from __future__ import annotations

# Bringing homes up to date (spec section 3, "Each tick"; CONTRACT section 14).
#
# Each tick, after tend and before anyone is ranked, the fleet reads every
# roster home's remote head under one bound: one GraphQL query through `gh`
# when it is there and the homes live on GitHub, otherwise one bounded
# `git ls-remote` per home, a few at a time. Only the homes whose head changed
# are fetched, each under 20 s, and fast-forwarded. A home whose local commits
# sit behind upstream commits that only add new files under inbox/ (a letter
# placed from elsewhere) is rebased onto them, which cannot conflict; a marker
# is written first, so a rebase a killed run left behind is aborted at the next
# sync. A home ahead of its upstream is pushed. A roster home with no clone is
# cloned under 60 s, and a clone that fails backs off like a failed beat.
#
# A home that cannot be brought up to date (diverged, a fetch or fast-forward
# that failed, a merge or rebase someone else left, a dirty home that needs a
# rebase) is held: its attempt record's "reported" list gains "out-of-date",
# which is the report, once, and keeps it from beats (citizen_pace.py due, rank
# and next read it) until a later sync finds it up to date. A home whose
# per-citizen lock is held, or that holds a .git/index.lock, is left for the
# next tick. No hook or fsmonitor from a home's own .git runs in these calls,
# and GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN never reach git or gh.

import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple

from . import attempts, clock, lock
from .homes import LinkRefused, git, index_lock_age, mid_merge, remove_regular, write_regular
from .tend import FLEET_EMAIL, FLEET_NAME

DEFAULT_BASE = "https://github.com/cambridgetcg"
BASE_ENV = "PACE_REMOTE_BASE"      # tests: a folder of bare repositories instead of GitHub
HEADS_BOUND = 60.0                 # every remote head, read under one bound
FETCH_BOUND = 20.0                 # each fetch, fast-forward, rebase or ls-remote
CLONE_BOUND = 60.0
PUSH_BOUND = 30.0
WORKERS = 8                        # ls-remote calls at a time
GRAPHQL_CHUNK = 250                # repositories per GraphQL query: today's 205 homes in one
REBASE_MARKER = "pace-rebase"      # .git/pace-rebase, written before a fleet-started rebase
HELD = "out-of-date"               # the attempt record's "reported" key of a held home
HELD_REASON = "out-of-date"        # the not-due reason citizen_pace.py gives a held home
NO_UPSTREAM = "no-upstream"
CLONE_ATTEMPT = "clone-"           # the attempt id of a failed clone: clone-<stamp>
CLONE_FAILED = "clone-failed"      # the attempt record's "reported" key of a home that cannot be cloned
CLONE_TMP = ".pace-clone"
HOLD_TAIL = " — no beats until it is brought up to date"
_SAFE = ("-c", "core.hooksPath=/dev/null", "-c", "core.fsmonitor=false")
_AS_FLEET = ("-c", f"user.name={FLEET_NAME}", "-c", f"user.email={FLEET_EMAIL}",
             "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "-c", "rebase.autoStash=false")
_OWNER = re.compile(r"https://github\.com/([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38})")
# a remote and branch the fleet will name on a git command line: never an option
_PLAIN_REMOTE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}")
_PLAIN_REF = re.compile(r"refs/(?:heads|remotes)/[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,199}")
_OID = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}(?:[0-9a-f]{24})?")
_REGULAR_MODES = ("100644", "100755")
_TOKENS = ("GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN")


def _git(home, *args, timeout: float = FETCH_BOUND):
    return git(home, *_SAFE, *args, timeout=timeout)


def _n(k: int, what: str) -> str:
    return f"{k} {what}" if k == 1 else f"{k} {what}s"


def _first_line(text: str, code: int) -> str:
    for ln in (text or "").splitlines():
        if ln.strip():
            return ln.strip()[:200]
    return f"git exited {code}"


# -- where homes come from --------------------------------------------------------

def remote_base() -> str:
    """Where homes are cloned from: PACE_REMOTE_BASE, else GitHub's cambridgetcg."""
    return (os.environ.get(BASE_ENV, "").strip() or DEFAULT_BASE).rstrip("/")


def clone_url(slug: str, base: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    return f"{(base or remote_base()).rstrip('/')}/citizen-{slug}.git"


def github_owner(base: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """The GitHub owner when the homes live on GitHub, else None (no GraphQL)."""
    m = _OWNER.fullmatch(base.rstrip("/"))
    return m.group(1) if m else None


# -- the hold ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def held(state, slug: str) -> bool:
    """A sync could not bring this home up to date: it gets no beats until a
    later sync can (a person's summons still passes)."""
    if not attempts.valid_slug(slug):
        return False
    return HELD in attempts.load(state, slug)["reported"]


def without_held(state, slugs: Iterable[str], cursor: int = 0) -> Tuple[List[str], int]:
    """The roster without its held homes, and the cursor moved to the first
    citizen not held at or after it, so ties keep their order from the cursor."""
    slugs = list(slugs)
    keep = [s for s in slugs if not held(state, s)]
    if len(keep) == len(slugs) or not keep:
        return keep, (cursor if len(keep) == len(slugs) else 0)
    n = len(slugs)
    for i in range(n):
        s = slugs[(cursor + i) % n]
        if s in keep:
            return keep, keep.index(s)
    return keep, 0


def _hold(state, slug: str, why: str) -> List[str]:
    if attempts.mark_reported(state, slug, HELD):
        return [f"{slug}: {why}{HOLD_TAIL}"]
    return []


def _release(state, slug: str) -> List[str]:
    if held(state, slug) and attempts.clear_reported(state, slug, HELD):
        return [f"{slug}: up to date again — its beats resume"]
    return []


# -- one home's git facts ------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Local:
    branch: str = ""        # refs/heads/<b> that HEAD is on; "" when detached
    head: str = ""
    upstream: str = ""      # the tracking ref, e.g. refs/remotes/origin/main
    remote: str = ""        # origin
    remoteref: str = ""     # refs/heads/main
    tracking: str = ""      # the tracking ref's commit; "" when there is none


def local_state(home) -> Local:
    r = _git(home, "for-each-ref", "--format=%(HEAD)%00%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(upstream)"
             "%00%(upstream:remotename)%00%(upstream:remoteref)", "refs/heads/")
    for line in r.stdout.splitlines() if r.returncode == 0 else []:
        parts = line.split("\0")
        if len(parts) == 6 and parts[0] == "*":
            loc = Local(*parts[1:])
            if loc.upstream:
                loc.tracking = _rev(home, loc.upstream)
            return loc
    return Local()


def _rev(home, ref: str) -> str:
    r = _git(home, "rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", f"{ref}^{{commit}}")
    return r.stdout.strip() if r.returncode == 0 else ""


def _counts(home, upstream: str) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int]]:
    """(behind, ahead) of HEAD against its upstream, or None."""
    r = _git(home, "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", f"{upstream}...HEAD")
    parts = r.stdout.split()
    if r.returncode != 0 or len(parts) != 2 or not all(p.isdigit() for p in parts):
        return None
    return int(parts[0]), int(parts[1])


def _mid_rebase(home) -> bool:
    g = Path(home) / ".git"
    return os.path.lexists(g / "rebase-merge") or os.path.lexists(g / "rebase-apply")


def upstream_adds(home, upstream: str) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    """The files the upstream side adds since the merge base, when that is all
    it does: each a new regular file under inbox/ that no local commit touches,
    with no merge among the local commits. None otherwise. A rebase onto such
    commits cannot conflict."""
    base = _git(home, "merge-base", "HEAD", upstream)
    if base.returncode != 0 or not _OID.fullmatch(base.stdout.strip()):
        return None
    b = base.stdout.strip()
    merges = _git(home, "rev-list", "--merges", "--count", f"{b}..HEAD")
    if merges.returncode != 0 or merges.stdout.strip() != "0":
        return None
    r = _git(home, "diff", "--raw", "-z", "--no-renames", "--no-ext-diff", b, upstream)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    tokens = r.stdout.split("\0")
    adds = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(tokens) and tokens[i]:
        meta = tokens[i].split()
        path = tokens[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(tokens) else ""
        i += 2
        if len(meta) < 5 or meta[4] != "A" or meta[1] not in _REGULAR_MODES \
                or not path.startswith("inbox/"):
            return None
        adds.append(path)
    mine = _git(home, "diff", "--name-only", "-z", "--no-renames", "--no-ext-diff", b, "HEAD")
    if mine.returncode != 0 or set(adds) & {p for p in mine.stdout.split("\0") if p}:
        return None
    return adds


def _dirty(home, adds: List[str]) -> bool:
    """Tracked changes, or an untracked file where the upstream adds one."""
    r = _git(home, "--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain=v1", "-z", "--untracked-files=no")
    if r.returncode != 0 or r.stdout.strip("\0"):
        return True
    return any(os.path.lexists(Path(home) / p) for p in adds)


# -- remote heads ---------------------------------------------------------------------

def _gh_env() -> dict:
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in _TOKENS}
    env.update(GH_PROMPT_DISABLED="1", GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER="1", GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0")
    return env


def _graphql_heads(gh: str, owner: str, items, deadline: float) -> Optional[Dict[str, str]]:
    """Each home's remote head from GitHub's default branch, by one query per
    GRAPHQL_CHUNK homes; only where that branch is the one the home tracks.
    None when no query could be read."""
    heads: Dict[str, str] = {}
    answered = False
    for k in range(0, len(items), GRAPHQL_CHUNK):
        chunk = items[k:k + GRAPHQL_CHUNK]
        left = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if left <= 0:
            break
        query = "query { " + " ".join(
            f'h{i}: repository(owner: "{owner}", name: "citizen-{slug}") '
            "{ defaultBranchRef { name target { oid } } }"
            for i, (slug, _home, _loc) in enumerate(chunk)) + " }"
        try:
            r = subprocess.run([gh, "api", "graphql", "-f", f"query={query}"], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=left, env=_gh_env())
            data = json.loads(r.stdout).get("data")
        except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
            continue
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            continue
        answered = True
        for i, (slug, _home, loc) in enumerate(chunk):
            ref = data.get(f"h{i}")
            ref = ref.get("defaultBranchRef") if isinstance(ref, dict) else None
            if not isinstance(ref, dict) or f"refs/heads/{ref.get('name')}" != loc.remoteref:
                continue
            oid = ref.get("target", {}).get("oid") if isinstance(ref.get("target"), dict) else None
            if isinstance(oid, str) and _OID.fullmatch(oid):
                heads[slug] = oid
    return heads if answered else None


def _ls_remote_heads(items, deadline: float) -> Dict[str, str]:
    """Each home's remote head by `git ls-remote`, WORKERS at a time, each call
    bounded by what is left of the one bound."""
    def one(item) -> Tuple[str, Optional[str]]:
        slug, home, loc = item
        left = deadline - time.monotonic()
        if left <= 0:
            return slug, None
        r = _git(home, "ls-remote", "-q", loc.remote, loc.remoteref, timeout=min(FETCH_BOUND, left))
        if r.returncode != 0:
            return slug, None
        for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
            oid, _tab, ref = line.partition("\t")
            if ref.strip() == loc.remoteref and _OID.fullmatch(oid.strip()):
                return slug, oid.strip()
        return slug, None

    heads: Dict[str, str] = {}
    if not items:
        return heads
    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(WORKERS, len(items))) as pool:
        for slug, oid in pool.map(one, items):
            if oid:
                heads[slug] = oid
    return heads


def read_heads(items, bound: float = HEADS_BOUND, gh: Optional[str] = None) -> Tuple[Dict[str, str], str]:
    """{slug: remote head} for items [(slug, home, Local)], all under one bound,
    and how they were read ("graphql", "ls-remote", "graphql+ls-remote" or
    "none"). gh: the gh program, used only when the homes live on GitHub."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + bound
    heads: Dict[str, str] = {}
    how = []
    owner = github_owner(remote_base())
    if gh and owner and items:
        how.append("graphql")
        heads.update(_graphql_heads(gh, owner, items, deadline) or {})
    rest = [it for it in items if it[0] not in heads]
    if rest:
        how.append("ls-remote")
        heads.update(_ls_remote_heads(rest, deadline))
    return heads, "+".join(how) or "none"


# -- cloning a missing home -------------------------------------------------------------

def _discard(p: Path) -> None:
    try:
        if stat.S_ISDIR(os.lstat(p).st_mode):
            shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=True)
        else:
            os.unlink(p)
    except OSError:
        pass


def clone_home(homes_dir, slug: str, base: Optional[str] = None,
               timeout: float = CLONE_BOUND) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
    """Clone citizen-<slug> into homes_dir under a bound, through a temporary
    folder renamed into place, so a clone cut short leaves no half home.
    (True, "") or (False, why)."""
    homes_dir = Path(homes_dir)
    homes_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest = homes_dir / f"citizen-{slug}"
    tmp = homes_dir / f".citizen-{slug}{CLONE_TMP}"
    _discard(tmp)
    r = git(homes_dir, *_SAFE, "clone", "-q", "--no-recurse-submodules", "--", clone_url(slug, base),
            tmp.name, timeout=timeout)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        _discard(tmp)
        why = f"timed out after {timeout:g} s" if r.returncode == 124 else _first_line(r.stderr, r.returncode)
        return False, why
    try:
        if os.path.lexists(dest):
            raise FileExistsError(f"{dest} appeared meanwhile")
        os.rename(tmp, dest)
    except OSError as e:
        _discard(tmp)
        return False, str(e)
    return True, ""


# -- the summary ----------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Summary:
    homes: int = 0
    heads: str = "none"
    heads_read: int = 0
    fetched: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    fast_forwarded: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    rebased: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    pushed: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    cloned: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    clone_failed: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    aborted: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    ahead: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)       # stay ahead: not pushed this tick
    diverged: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    held: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)        # get no beats until a sync brings them up to date
    skipped: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)     # left for the next tick
    lines: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        d = {k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if k != "lines"}
        return {k: (list(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v) for k, v in d.items()}


# -- one home ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _prepare(home: Path, slug: str, state, now, s: Summary) -> Optional[Local]:
    """What can be decided without the network. Returns the home's git facts
    when it may be brought up to date this tick, else None."""
    if not os.path.lexists(home):
        if attempts.backing_off(attempts.load(state, slug), now):
            s.skipped.append(slug)
            return None
        ok, why = clone_home(home.parent, slug)
        if ok:
            s.cloned.append(slug)
            s.lines.append(f"{slug}: cloned")
            s.lines += _release(state, slug)
            attempts.clear_reported(state, slug, CLONE_FAILED)
        else:
            attempts.record_outcome(state, slug, f"{CLONE_ATTEMPT}{clock.stamp(now)}", "home-failed", now)
            s.clone_failed.append(slug)
            s.lines.append(f"{slug}: clone failed — {why}; backed off like a failed beat")
            if attempts.mark_reported(state, slug, CLONE_FAILED):
                s.lines.append(f"{slug}: cannot be cloned — it gets no beats until a clone succeeds "
                               "(reported once)")
        return None
    git_dir = home / ".git"
    if os.path.islink(home) or not os.path.isdir(home) or os.path.islink(git_dir) \
            or not os.path.isdir(git_dir):
        s.held.append(slug)
        s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "not a clone")
        return None
    if lock.held(state, slug, now):
        s.skipped.append(slug)
        s.lines.append(f"{slug}: its lock is held — not synced this tick")
        return None
    marker = git_dir / REBASE_MARKER
    if os.path.lexists(marker):
        if _mid_rebase(home):
            r = _git(home, "rebase", "--abort")
            if r.returncode != 0 and _mid_rebase(home):
                s.held.append(slug)
                s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "a fleet rebase left in progress could not be aborted")
                return None
            s.aborted.append(slug)
            s.lines.append(f"{slug}: a fleet rebase left in progress was aborted")
        _discard(marker)
    if mid_merge(home):
        s.held.append(slug)
        s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "a merge or rebase is in progress")
        return None
    if index_lock_age(home) is not None:
        s.skipped.append(slug)
        s.lines.append(f"{slug}: .git/index.lock is there — not synced this tick")
        return None
    loc = local_state(home)
    if not loc.branch:
        s.held.append(slug)
        s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "HEAD is not on a branch")
        return None
    if not loc.upstream:
        if attempts.mark_reported(state, slug, NO_UPSTREAM):
            s.lines.append(f"{slug}: has no upstream — its beats stay local")
        s.lines += _release(state, slug)
        return None
    if not (_PLAIN_REMOTE.fullmatch(loc.remote) and _PLAIN_REF.fullmatch(loc.remoteref)
            and loc.remoteref.startswith("refs/heads/") and _PLAIN_REF.fullmatch(loc.upstream)):
        s.held.append(slug)
        s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "its upstream is not a plain remote branch")
        return None
    return loc


def _push(home: Path, slug: str, loc: Local, s: Summary) -> None:
    counts = _counts(home, loc.upstream)
    ahead = counts[1] if counts else 0
    r = _git(home, "push", "-q", "--no-verify", loc.remote, f"HEAD:{loc.remoteref}", timeout=PUSH_BOUND)
    if r.returncode == 0:
        s.pushed.append(slug)
        s.lines.append(f"{slug}: pushed {_n(ahead, 'commit')}")
    else:
        s.ahead.append(slug)


def _rebase(home: Path, loc: Local) -> str:
    """Rebase the local commits onto the upstream as the fleet (authors kept),
    with the marker written first; "" when done, else why (and it is aborted)."""
    marker = home / ".git" / REBASE_MARKER
    write_regular(marker, f"{clock.stamp(clock.now())} pid {os.getpid()}\n")
    r = _git(home, *_AS_FLEET, "rebase", "-q", "--no-verify", loc.upstream)
    if r.returncode == 0:
        remove_regular(marker)
        return ""
    why = f"timed out after {FETCH_BOUND:g} s" if r.returncode == 124 else _first_line(r.stderr, r.returncode)
    a = _git(home, "rebase", "--abort")
    if a.returncode == 0 or not _mid_rebase(home):
        remove_regular(marker)
    return why


def _bring(home: Path, slug: str, state, loc: Local, oid: Optional[str], s: Summary) -> None:
    """Fetch when the remote head moved, then fast-forward, rebase onto letters,
    or push, or hold the home."""
    if oid and oid != loc.tracking:
        r = _git(home, "fetch", "-q", "--no-recurse-submodules", loc.remote)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            s.held.append(slug)
            s.lines += _hold(state, slug, f"fetch failed ({_first_line(r.stderr, r.returncode)})")
            return
        s.fetched.append(slug)
        loc.tracking = _rev(home, loc.upstream)
    if not loc.tracking:
        return
    if loc.head == loc.tracking:
        s.lines += _release(state, slug)
        return
    counts = _counts(home, loc.upstream)
    if counts is None:
        s.held.append(slug)
        s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "cannot be compared with its upstream")
        return
    behind, ahead = counts
    if behind and not ahead:
        r = _git(home, "merge", "-q", "--ff-only", loc.upstream)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            s.held.append(slug)
            s.lines += _hold(state, slug, f"fast-forward failed ({_first_line(r.stderr, r.returncode)})")
            return
        s.fast_forwarded.append(slug)
        s.lines.append(f"{slug}: fast-forwarded {_n(behind, 'commit')}")
        s.lines += _release(state, slug)
        return
    if behind and ahead:
        adds = upstream_adds(home, loc.upstream)
        if adds is None:
            s.diverged.append(slug)
            s.held.append(slug)
            s.lines += _hold(state, slug, f"diverged ({ahead} local, {_n(behind, 'upstream commit')})")
            return
        if _dirty(home, adds):
            s.diverged.append(slug)
            s.held.append(slug)
            s.lines += _hold(state, slug, "diverged, with uncommitted changes, so not rebased")
            return
        why = _rebase(home, loc)
        if why:
            s.diverged.append(slug)
            s.held.append(slug)
            s.lines += _hold(state, slug, f"rebase onto upstream letters failed and was aborted ({why})")
            return
        s.rebased.append(slug)
        s.lines.append(f"{slug}: rebased {_n(ahead, 'local commit')} onto {_n(behind, 'upstream commit')} "
                       f"that only {'adds' if behind == 1 else 'add'} letters")
    s.lines += _release(state, slug)
    if oid:
        _push(home, slug, loc, s)
    else:
        s.ahead.append(slug)


def sync_homes(homes_dir, slugs: Iterable[str], state, bound: float = HEADS_BOUND,
               now=None, gh: Optional[str] = None) -> Summary:
    """Bring every roster home up to date (`citizen_pace.py sync`). Remote heads
    are read once for all homes under `bound` seconds; each home is then
    fetched, fast-forwarded, rebased onto letters placed elsewhere, pushed,
    cloned, held or left for the next tick. Returns the summary and its log lines."""
    now = now or clock.now()
    homes_dir = Path(homes_dir)
    slugs = list(slugs)
    s = Summary(homes=len(slugs))
    ready = []
    for slug in slugs:
        home = homes_dir / f"citizen-{slug}"
        try:
            loc = _prepare(home, slug, state, now, s)
        except (OSError, ValueError, LinkRefused) as e:
            s.skipped.append(slug)
            s.lines.append(f"{slug}: not synced this tick — {e}")
            continue
        if loc is not None:
            ready.append((slug, home, loc))
    heads, s.heads = read_heads(ready, bound, gh) if ready else ({}, "none")
    s.heads_read = len(heads)
    for slug, home, loc in ready:
        try:
            _bring(home, slug, state, loc, heads.get(slug), s)
        except (OSError, ValueError, LinkRefused) as e:
            s.skipped.append(slug)
            s.lines.append(f"{slug}: not synced this tick — {e}")
    return s
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the host probe**

Create `tools/citizen_pace_lib/probe.py`:

```python
from __future__ import annotations

# The host probe (spec section 3, "A beat that does not land"; CONTRACT section
# 14). Whether a failed beat was the home's or the host's is decided by the
# fleet, with a probe that touches no home: a write and delete under the attempt
# records' folder, citizen_pace.py and citizen-gates.sh present beside each
# other, and one fixed prompt to the configured model server (the same MLX_PORT
# and REFLECT_MODEL the beats use) that must answer within 60 s. Any HTTP 200
# whose body parses as JSON passes. The fleet runs it at the start of each tick
# and again after any failed beat; a failed probe charges no citizen.

import json
import os
import socket
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Mapping, Optional

PROBE_TEXT = "Reply with one word: here."
PROBE_TOKENS = 4
PROBE_TIMEOUT = 60.0
DEFAULT_PORT = "8800"            # citizen-reflect.sh's MLX_PORT default
TOOL_FILES = ("citizen_pace.py", "citizen-gates.sh")
READ_LIMIT = 1_000_000


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Probe:
    ok: bool
    line: str


def check_state(state) -> str:
    """"" when a file can be written and deleted under the state folder (made
    when missing), else why not."""
    p = Path(state) / f".probe-{os.getpid()}"
    try:
        os.makedirs(str(state), exist_ok=True)
        if os.path.lexists(p):
            os.unlink(p)             # a probe killed before its delete; a link is removed, not followed
        fd = os.open(str(p), os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
        try:
            os.write(fd, b"probe\n")
        finally:
            os.close(fd)
        os.unlink(p)
    except OSError as e:
        return f"cannot write and delete {p} ({e.strerror or e})"
    return ""


def check_tools(tools_dir) -> str:
    """"" when citizen_pace.py and citizen-gates.sh sit in tools_dir, else what is missing."""
    for name in TOOL_FILES:
        if not os.path.isfile(Path(tools_dir) / name):
            return f"{name} is missing from {tools_dir}"
    return ""


def request_for(env: Mapping[str, str]):
    """(url, payload) of the probe's one request, or (None, why) for a setting
    no beat could use."""
    port = (env.get("MLX_PORT") or DEFAULT_PORT).strip()
    if not port.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(port) <= 65535:
        return None, f"MLX_PORT {port!r} is not a port"
    model = (env.get("REFLECT_MODEL") or "").strip()
    if model.endswith(":cloud"):
        return None, f"REFLECT_MODEL {model!r} is a cloud model; the free lane is local only"
    if model:
        return (f"http://127.0.0.1:{int(port)}/v1/chat/completions",
                {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": PROBE_TEXT}], "max_tokens": PROBE_TOKENS,
                 "model": model})
    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{int(port)}/inference", {"prompt": PROBE_TEXT, "max_tokens": PROBE_TOKENS}


def _timed_out(e: BaseException) -> bool:
    reason = getattr(e, "reason", None)
    return isinstance(e, socket.timeout) or isinstance(reason, socket.timeout) \
        or "timed out" in str(e)


def ask_model(env: Mapping[str, str], timeout: float = PROBE_TIMEOUT) -> str:
    """"" when the model server answers the probe's prompt with HTTP 200 and a
    JSON body within timeout seconds, else why not. No proxy is used."""
    url, payload = request_for(env)
    if url is None:
        return payload
    box: dict = {}

    def run() -> None:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
        try:
            with opener.open(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
                box["status"] = resp.status
                box["body"] = resp.read(READ_LIMIT)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            box["status"] = e.code
            e.close()
        except Exception as e:      # noqa: BLE001 — any failure to answer is the host's
            box["error"] = e

    worker = threading.Thread(target=run, daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    worker.join(timeout + 1)
    if worker.is_alive() or ("error" in box and _timed_out(box["error"])):
        return f"the model server gave no answer within {timeout:g} s"
    if "error" in box:
        e = box["error"]
        return f"the model server could not be reached at {url} ({getattr(e, 'reason', e)})"
    if box.get("status") != 200:
        return f"the model server answered HTTP {box.get('status')}"
    try:
        json.loads(box.get("body", b"").decode("utf-8"))
    except ValueError:
        return "the model server's answer is not JSON"
    return ""


def probe(state, tools_dir, env: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
          timeout: float = PROBE_TIMEOUT) -> Probe:
    """The host probe: the state folder, then the tools, then the model; the
    first that fails is the line."""
    env = os.environ if env is None else env
    why = check_state(state) or check_tools(tools_dir)
    if why:
        return Probe(False, f"probe: failed — {why}")
    t = time.monotonic()
    why = ask_model(env, timeout)
    if why:
        return Probe(False, f"probe: failed — {why}")
    return Probe(True, f"probe: ok — {state} writable, {' and '.join(TOOL_FILES)} present, "
                       f"the model answered in {time.monotonic() - t:.1f} s")
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the command line**

Create `tools/citizen_pace.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""citizen_pace.py — each citizen keeps its own pace (pace/1).

The one command line over tools/citizen_pace_lib/ that the beat scripts call
(spec section 7; CONTRACT sections 11 and 14). Run it as
`python3 -I tools/citizen_pace.py <command> ...`: it puts its own real folder
first on sys.path, so it works isolated and never imports from the folder it is
run in. Its exit codes are its own, read only by the shell gates: 0 ok or due,
4 not due, busy or a host fault, 2 a usage error or a home that cannot be read.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)))

import argparse  # noqa: E402
import json  # noqa: E402
import math  # noqa: E402
import shutil  # noqa: E402
from pathlib import Path  # noqa: E402

from citizen_pace_lib import (answer, attempts, clock, due, homes, lock, paragraph, probe,  # noqa: E402
                              sync, tend)
from citizen_pace_lib import record as records  # noqa: E402

OK, NOT, ERROR = 0, 4, 2
TOOLS = Path(os.path.realpath(__file__)).parent
ANSWER_LIMIT = 1_000_000
# the outcomes of a beat whose model was shown the whole pace paragraph
SHOWN_PARAGRAPH = attempts.LANDED + ("summoned",)
# why a roster home gets no beats, reported once by the fleet's ranking (spec section 3)
NO_BEATS = {"no-soul": "it has no {slug}.md",
             "links": "a pace path is a symlink or not of its kind",
             "blocked": "its record cannot become v2 until a person has looked",
             "error": "its home could not be read",
             "unreadable": "its pace cannot be read, so it gets no set beats; only a letter wakes it"}
NO_BEATS_KEY = "no-beats-"
# reasons that say nothing about whether a pace can be read: an unreadable pace's
# report is kept through them, so a letter waking that citizen does not report it again
PACE_SILENT = ("letter", "floor", "backing-off", "mid-merge", "no-home", "out-of-date")

USAGE = """usage: citizen_pace.py <command> [arguments]

commands:
  due <home> --state <dir> [--summoned] [--record <f>] [--no-seed]
  rank <homes-dir> --roster <f> --state <dir> [--record <f>] [--cursor N]
  next <homes-dir> --roster <f> --state <dir> [--record <f>] [--cursor N]
  paragraph <home> [--shown <rel> ...] [--record <f>] [--state <dir>]
  apply <home> <answer-file> --kind K [--shown <rel> ...] [--record <f>] [--state <dir>]
  record <slug> --state <dir> --attempt <id> --outcome <o> [--shown <rel> ...]
  outcome <slug> --state <dir> --attempt <id>
  lock <slug> --state <dir> --pid <pid> [--bound S]
  unlock <slug> --state <dir> [--pid <pid>]
  probe --state <dir> [--timeout S]
  guard-restore <home> --state <dir>
  tend <homes-dir> --roster <f> --state <dir>
  sync <homes-dir> --roster <f> --state <dir> [--bound S]
  migrate --heard-late <homes-dir> [--record <f>] [--state <dir>] [--commit]
  plan <days> <homes-dir> --roster <f> [--cap N] [--tick-hours H]
       [--letters <f> --deliver-at <t> [--per-run N]] [--out <dir>] [--record <f>]
       [--state <dir>] [--cursor N]
  rollback-drill <homes-dir> --roster <f> --days N [--cap N] [--tick-hours H] [--cursor N]
  rollback-prepare <homes-dir> --roster <f> [--state <dir>] [--no-push]

exit: 0 ok or due; 4 not due, busy or a host fault; 2 a usage error, or a home
that cannot be read
"""


class Usage(Exception):
    """Arguments that parse but do not go together."""


def _parser(cmd: str, about: str) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    return argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=f"citizen_pace.py {cmd}", description=about)


def _shown(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    p.add_argument("--shown", action="extend", nargs="+", default=[], metavar="REL",
                   help="what the beat showed: inbox/<letter>.md, or SHOW.md")


def _record_opt(p: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
    p.add_argument("--record", help="the record file (default: citizens-pace-record.json)")


def _roster_opts(p: argparse.ArgumentParser, state: bool = True) -> None:
    p.add_argument("homes_dir")
    p.add_argument("--roster", required=True)
    if state:
        p.add_argument("--state", required=True, help="the attempt records (memory/.fleet-last)")


def _record_file(a) -> dict:
    return records.load_record(Path(a.record) if a.record else None)


def _home(a):
    home = Path(a.home)
    return home, homes.slug_of(home)


# -- the commands --------------------------------------------------------------------

def p_due():
    p = _parser("due", "Is this citizen due now? Prints the reason and how overdue.")
    p.add_argument("home")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--summoned", action="store_true", help="a person's summons (BEAT_SUMMONS=1)")
    p.add_argument("--no-seed", action="store_true", help="never start a clock in the attempt record")
    _record_opt(p)
    return p


def cmd_due(a) -> int:
    home, slug = _home(a)
    rec = _record_file(a)
    now = clock.now()
    d = due.due_for_home(home, slug, a.state, rec, now, summoned=a.summoned, write_seed=not a.no_seed)
    if d.due and not a.summoned and sync.held(a.state, slug):
        d = due.Due(False, sync.HELD_REASON)
    print(json.dumps(d.to_json(now), sort_keys=True))
    if d.reason == "error":
        print(f"due: {home} could not be read", file=sys.stderr)
        return ERROR
    return OK if d.due else NOT


def p_rank():
    p = _parser("rank", "The due citizens, most overdue first: slug, reason, seconds overdue.")
    _roster_opts(p)
    _record_opt(p)
    p.add_argument("--cursor", type=int, default=0)
    return p


def _report_no_beats(state, assessed) -> None:
    """Once per home and reason, on stderr: a roster citizen that gets no beats
    (no soul, a linked pace path, a blocked record, a home that cannot be read,
    a pace that cannot be read). The report is forgotten when the reason goes,
    so it is made again if it comes back; an unreadable pace's is kept through
    the reasons that say nothing about the pace (a letter waking it, its floor)."""
    for slug, d in assessed:
        keys = [k for k in attempts.load(state, slug)["reported"] if k.startswith(NO_BEATS_KEY)]
        want = NO_BEATS_KEY + d.reason if d.reason in NO_BEATS else None
        for k in keys:
            if k == want or (want is None and k == NO_BEATS_KEY + "unreadable"
                             and d.reason in PACE_SILENT):
                continue
            attempts.clear_reported(state, slug, k)
        if want and want not in keys and attempts.mark_reported(state, slug, want):
            why = NO_BEATS[d.reason].format(slug=slug)
            print(f"{slug}: gets no beats — {why} (reported once)", file=sys.stderr)


def cmd_rank(a) -> int:
    now = clock.now()
    slugs = due.read_roster(a.roster)
    assessed = due.assess(a.homes_dir, slugs, a.state, _record_file(a), now, write_seed=True)
    _report_no_beats(a.state, assessed)
    # ordered exactly as due.rank orders them (its own helpers), without held homes
    for slug, d in due._ranked(assessed, due._order(slugs, a.cursor)):
        if not sync.held(a.state, slug):
            print(f"{slug}\t{d.reason}\t{d.overdue_s(now)}")
    return OK


def p_next():
    p = _parser("next", "fleet-status.sh's 'next to wake' line. Writes nothing.")
    _roster_opts(p)
    _record_opt(p)
    p.add_argument("--cursor", type=int, default=0)
    return p


def cmd_next(a) -> int:
    slugs, cursor = sync.without_held(a.state, due.read_roster(a.roster), a.cursor)
    print(due.next_line(a.homes_dir, slugs, a.state, _record_file(a), clock.now(), cursor=cursor))
    return OK


def p_paragraph():
    p = _parser("paragraph", "The pace paragraph for this beat.")
    p.add_argument("home")
    _shown(p)
    _record_opt(p)
    p.add_argument("--state", help="the attempt records, for their notices")
    return p


def cmd_paragraph(a) -> int:
    home, slug = _home(a)
    rec = attempts.load(a.state, slug) if a.state else None
    print(paragraph.paragraph_for(home, slug, _record_file(a), confirm_beat=due.WAKE_CONFIRM_BEAT,
                                  shown=a.shown, rec=rec, now=clock.now()))
    return OK


def p_apply():
    p = _parser("apply", "Apply a landed beat's answer to its home; prints what changed.")
    p.add_argument("home")
    p.add_argument("answer_file")
    p.add_argument("--kind", required=True, choices=answer.BEAT_KINDS)
    _shown(p)
    _record_opt(p)
    p.add_argument("--state", help="the attempt records: the last landed beat before this one")
    return p


def cmd_apply(a) -> int:
    home, slug = _home(a)
    with open(a.answer_file, "rb") as fh:
        text = fh.read(ANSWER_LIMIT).decode("utf-8", "replace")
    # run before record, so the attempt record still holds the previous landed beat
    since = attempts.load(a.state, slug)["last_beat"] if a.state else None
    res = answer.apply_answer(home, slug, text, a.shown, a.kind, clock.now(), _record_file(a),
                              since=since)
    print(json.dumps(res.to_json(), sort_keys=True))
    return OK


def p_record():
    p = _parser("record", "Record what one attempt came to.")
    p.add_argument("slug")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--attempt", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--outcome", required=True, choices=attempts.OUTCOMES)
    _shown(p)
    return p


def cmd_record(a) -> int:
    now = clock.now()
    attempts.record_outcome(a.state, a.slug, a.attempt, a.outcome, now)
    if a.outcome in SHOWN_PARAGRAPH and not paragraph.shows_pace_letter(a.shown):
        # its paragraph showed the attempt record's notices, once
        attempts.clear_notices(a.state, a.slug, upto=now)
    if a.outcome == "busy" and attempts.report_busy(a.state, a.slug):
        print(f"{a.slug}: busy on two ticks running (reported once)")
    return OK


def p_outcome():
    p = _parser("outcome", "The outcome an attempt recorded, or 'missing'.")
    p.add_argument("slug")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--attempt", required=True)
    return p


def cmd_outcome(a) -> int:
    print(attempts.outcome_for(a.state, a.slug, a.attempt))
    return OK


def p_lock():
    p = _parser("lock", "Take the citizen's lock: 0 taken, 4 held by another run.")
    p.add_argument("slug")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--pid", type=int, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--bound", help="the beat bound in seconds (default FLEET_BEAT_BOUND_SEC, else 600)")
    return p


def cmd_lock(a) -> int:
    t = lock.take(a.state, a.slug, a.pid, bound=None if a.bound is None else lock.beat_bound(a.bound))
    if t.reclaimed:
        print(f"{a.slug}: a stale lock was reclaimed ({t.reclaimed})")
    if t.got:
        return OK
    h = t.holder
    who = f"pid {h.pid}" if h is not None and h.pid else "no recorded pid"
    since = f", started {h.started}" if h is not None and h.started else ""
    print(f"{a.slug}: its lock is held by {who}{since}")
    return NOT


def p_unlock():
    p = _parser("unlock", "Release the citizen's lock (with --pid, only that holder's).")
    p.add_argument("slug")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--pid", type=int)
    return p


def cmd_unlock(a) -> int:
    lock.release(a.state, a.slug, a.pid)
    return OK


def p_probe():
    p = _parser("probe", "The host probe: 0 the host can beat, 4 a host fault.")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--timeout", type=float, default=probe.PROBE_TIMEOUT)
    return p


def cmd_probe(a) -> int:
    if not (a.timeout > 0 and math.isfinite(a.timeout)):
        raise Usage("--timeout must be a number of seconds above 0")
    result = probe.probe(a.state, TOOLS, timeout=a.timeout)
    print(result.line)
    return OK if result.ok else NOT


def p_guard_restore():
    p = _parser("guard-restore", "After a beat with tools: put the pace files back as HEAD has them.")
    p.add_argument("home")
    p.add_argument("--state", required=True)
    return p


def cmd_guard_restore(a) -> int:
    home, slug = _home(a)
    paths = tend.guard_restore(home, a.state)
    if paths:
        print(tend.guard_line(slug, paths))
    return OK


def p_tend():
    p = _parser("tend", "Restore a killed beat's leftovers (the first tick: commit the old code's).")
    _roster_opts(p)
    return p


def cmd_tend(a) -> int:
    for line in tend.tend_homes(a.homes_dir, due.read_roster(a.roster), a.state):
        print(line)
    return OK


def p_sync():
    p = _parser("sync", "Bring the roster's homes up to date; log lines, then a JSON summary.")
    _roster_opts(p)
    p.add_argument("--bound", type=float, default=sync.HEADS_BOUND,
                   help="seconds to read every remote head in (default 60)")
    return p


def cmd_sync(a) -> int:
    if not (a.bound > 0 and math.isfinite(a.bound)):
        raise Usage("--bound must be a number of seconds above 0")
    s = sync.sync_homes(a.homes_dir, due.read_roster(a.roster), a.state, bound=a.bound,
                        gh=shutil.which("gh"))
    for line in s.lines:
        print(line)
    print(json.dumps(s.to_json(), sort_keys=True))
    return OK


def p_migrate():
    p = _parser("migrate", "Hear the unheard from their own answers, once, as the fleet.")
    p.add_argument("--heard-late", action="store_true", help="the heard-late step (spec section 5)")
    p.add_argument("homes_dir")
    _record_opt(p)
    p.add_argument("--state", help="the attempt records: the lock check and reporting once")
    p.add_argument("--commit", action="store_true", help="write and commit; without it, a dry run")
    return p


def cmd_migrate(a) -> int:
    if not a.heard_late:
        raise Usage("give --heard-late, the one migration there is")
    if a.commit and not a.state:
        raise Usage("--commit needs --state <dir>")
    # a dry run writes nothing, so it is given no state to report into
    for line in records.migrate_all(a.homes_dir, _record_file(a), clock.now(), a.commit,
                                    state=a.state if a.commit else None):
        print(line)
    return OK


def p_rollback_prepare():
    p = _parser("rollback-prepare", "Set unread pace letters aside before the old code returns.")
    _roster_opts(p, state=False)
    p.add_argument("--state", help="the attempt records, so a home whose lock is held is left")
    p.add_argument("--no-push", action="store_true", help="commit the markers, push nothing")
    return p


def cmd_rollback_prepare(a) -> int:
    for line in tend.rollback_prepare(a.homes_dir, due.read_roster(a.roster), state=a.state,
                                      now=clock.now(), push=not a.no_push):
        print(line)
    return OK


COMMANDS = {
    "due": (p_due, cmd_due), "rank": (p_rank, cmd_rank), "next": (p_next, cmd_next),
    "paragraph": (p_paragraph, cmd_paragraph), "apply": (p_apply, cmd_apply),
    "record": (p_record, cmd_record), "outcome": (p_outcome, cmd_outcome),
    "lock": (p_lock, cmd_lock), "unlock": (p_unlock, cmd_unlock), "probe": (p_probe, cmd_probe),
    "guard-restore": (p_guard_restore, cmd_guard_restore), "tend": (p_tend, cmd_tend),
    "sync": (p_sync, cmd_sync), "migrate": (p_migrate, cmd_migrate),
    "rollback-prepare": (p_rollback_prepare, cmd_rollback_prepare),
}


def _utf8_output() -> None:
    """Pace words hold '—' and quoted words: write UTF-8 whatever the locale."""
    for stream in (sys.stdout, sys.stderr):
        try:
            stream.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        except (AttributeError, ValueError):
            pass


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    _utf8_output()
    if not argv:
        sys.stderr.write(USAGE)
        return ERROR
    cmd, rest = argv[0], argv[1:]
    if cmd in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
        sys.stdout.write(USAGE)
        return OK
    if cmd in ("plan", "rollback-drill"):
        from citizen_pace_lib import plan    # the simulator loads only when asked for
        return plan.cli_plan(rest) if cmd == "plan" else plan.cli_rollback_drill(rest)
    if cmd not in COMMANDS:
        sys.stderr.write(f"citizen_pace.py: unknown command {cmd!r}\n\n{USAGE}")
        return ERROR
    build, run = COMMANDS[cmd]
    try:
        a = build().parse_args(rest)
    except SystemExit as e:
        return OK if e.code in (0, None) else ERROR
    try:
        return run(a)
    except Usage as e:
        print(f"citizen_pace.py {cmd}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return ERROR
    except (ValueError, OSError, homes.LinkRefused, tend.TendError) as e:
        print(f"{cmd}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return ERROR


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

### Task 9: The gates and citizen-beat.sh's guards

This task changes the shell gate every launcher sources and the one beat script that has tools.
`tools/citizen-gates.sh` (PR #24's single rest gate) learns that a `REST` whose text says "letters
wait" keeps rest even with unread mail (spec section 2, "Markers"), so the marker-only readers on
this code (`citizen-beat.sh`, the parade, `fleet-status.sh`) honour `asleep, letters wait`; an older
checkout without this change still wakes such a citizen on any letter, as the spec says. It gains `pace_due`, the free lane's gate (spec section 7): it asks
`citizen_pace.py due` by absolute path under `python3 -I`, with the attempt record in
`$LOVE/memory/.fleet-last`, and anything but "due" (exit 0) is not due, an error included. Its own
inline Python runs isolated too.

`tools/citizen-beat.sh` keeps the guards spec section 3 ("The old paid lane") gives it, because its
beats have edit tools inside the home, carry no pace paragraph and never show or mark a letter:

- it takes the per-citizen lock before anything touches the home (a second run is busy and exits 0);
- without a person's summons (`BEAT_SUMMONS=1`, never with `BEAT_BUDGET_ENFORCE=1`) it refuses a home
  with unread mail and exits 0: letters wait for the free reflect lane;
- after every beat, `citizen_pace.py guard-restore` puts `CADENCE.md`, `REST`, `EVENT-ONLY` and
  `inbox/` back as HEAD has them before the commit, logs what it put back once, and leaves a notice in
  the attempt record, so the next free beat's paragraph tells the citizen once;
- its inline Python runs with `-I`, so a `json.py` in the home (its working folder) is never imported;
- its result file is its own: `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/beat-$NAME.XXXXXX"`, with the X's last. PR #24's
  name ended in `.json` after them, which macOS's `mktemp` leaves as written, so a file left by a
  killed beat made every later beat of that citizen run no `claude`. A beat that cannot make the file
  is refused (exit 1), and the file is removed on any exit.

Nothing here touches `citizen-reflect.sh`, `citizen-fleet.sh`, `fleet-status.sh` or the parade (spec
section 7 leaves the parade unchanged); Tasks 10 and 11 wire `pace_due` and the CLI into the first
three. Two of PR #24's assertions change, each named in this task's commit (spec section 8):
`TestBeat.test_unread_letter_wakes_rest` is retired for `test_unread_letter_is_refused_without_a_summons`,
and `TestParade.test_parade_lines_up_only_citizens_not_resting` now expects the lettered home to be
lined up, refused by `citizen-beat.sh` with no `claude` run, and logged as walked. Every other PR #24
test passes unchanged.

- Modify: `tests/test_citizen_live_lane.py` (two PR #24 tests, by name, in Step 2)
- Test: `tests/test_citizen_pace_shell_gates.py` (new)

- Produces, `tools/citizen-gates.sh` (sourced, never run):
  - `has_mail <home>`: unchanged (a rollback marker counts as seen, as PR #24 reads it).
  - `unread_mail <home>`: true when `has_mail`, or when a regular letter's regular `.seen-` marker

  - `rest_letters_wait <home>`: true when `REST` is a regular file (never read through a link, never
    opened as a FIFO) whose text contains `letters wait`, in any case, as `cadence.py` reads it.
  - `keeps_rest <home>`: as PR #24's, except that a letters-wait `REST` keeps rest with unread mail.
    Only `REST`'s text counts; a linked `REST` still counts as a marker and is never read.
  - `pace_cli <command> [args]`: `python3 -I "$_gates_dir/citizen_pace.py" "$@"`, the CLI beside this
    file by absolute path, from any working folder. Tasks 10 and 11 call the CLI through it.
  - `pace_due <home> [--summoned]`: true only when `pace_cli due <home> [--summoned] --state
    "${LOVE:-${LOVE_DIR:-$HOME/love-unlimited}}/memory/.fleet-last"` exits 0; its stderr is dropped.
    It sets the global `PACE_DUE` to the JSON line `due` printed (`{"due", "next_at", "overdue_s",
    "reason", "since"}`), or `""` when it printed none. Call it in the script's own shell (not inside
    `$(...)`) for `PACE_DUE` to be seen. It writes the clock start (no `--no-seed`): the reflect gate
    is one of the two writers spec section 3 allows.
  - `pace_reason`: prints the `reason` in `PACE_DUE` (`schedule`, `letter`, `show-back`, `summoned`,
    or why not), or prints nothing and returns 1. Task 10 reads the beat's kind from it.
  - `spent_today <ledger>`, `budget_reached <ledger> <budget>`: unchanged, but run as `python3 -I -`.
  - Globals `_gates_self` and `_gates_dir` (this file's folder, absolute).
- Produces, `tools/citizen-beat.sh`: the order is HALT, the budget wall (exit 3), the lock, clone and
  fast-forward, `WILL.md`, `--clone-only`, the rest gate, the unread-mail refusal, the beat,
  `guard-restore`, the ledger, the commit (the pace paths are kept out of it), the push; the lock is
  released, and the beat's result file removed, on exit (`unlock --pid $$`). It writes no outcome to
  the attempt record, `busy` included.
  Its log lines, after `[<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>] `:
  - `<slug>: a stale lock was reclaimed (<why>)` (the beat goes on);
  - `<slug>: its lock is held by pid <pid>, started <stamp> — busy, no beat` (exit 0);
  - `ERROR: <name>'s lock could not be taken — beat refused (<why>)` (exit 1);
  - `<name> rests by its own standing choice (REST or EVENT-ONLY) — no beat` (exit 0; PR #24's line
    without its "no unread mail", which a letters-wait rest no longer needs);
  - `<name> rests by its own standing choice; a human present summons it for one beat` (unchanged);
  - `<name> has unread mail — letters wait for its free beat, so it gets no beat with tools without a
    person's summons` (exit 0);
  - `<name> has unread mail; a person's summons gives it this beat with tools all the same (its letters
    stay unread for its free beat)`;
  - `<slug>: pace files put back after a beat with tools: <paths>` (`tend.guard_line`, once);
  - `<name>: its pace files could not be checked after its beat — they are kept out of its commit
    (<why>)`;
  - `ERROR: <name>'s beat has no file for its result — beat refused` (exit 1, no `claude` run).
  Its commit subject stays `beat: <name> lived a free beat (<date>)`, untagged, as spec section 9 step
  6 expects of it.

Decisions, and why:

- **citizen-beat.sh writes nothing to the attempt record but guard-restore's notice, not even
  `busy`.** Spec section 3 makes the record "one record shared by the fleet and
  `citizen-reflect.sh`", and a hand-run of `citizen-beat.sh` "does not move the fleet's clock". The
  record keeps one attempt, so a hand-run's `busy` written while a fleet child holds the lock would
  replace that child's outcome: the fleet would read `missing`, probe, and back off a beat that landed.
  The busy run is logged instead.
- **The lock comes after HALT and the budget wall, before the clone and the fast-forward.** Those two
  read no home; the fetch and merge write one, and the fleet's sync skips a locked home, so they
  belong inside the lock. A lock that cannot be taken (no `citizen_pace.py` or `python3`, a state
  path that is not a folder) refuses the beat with exit 1: fail closed. Before, such a host beat and
  logged the cost as unknown.
- **The rest gate first, then the unread-mail refusal.** A letters-wait `REST` with mail logs that
  it rests; a plain `REST` that mail would wake, an `EVENT-ONLY` home (letters wait for an awake
  citizen's beat) and a home with no marker are refused for their mail. A summons passes both, by
  PR #24's rule: `BEAT_SUMMONS=1` without `BEAT_BUDGET_ENFORCE=1`, so the parade never summons.
- **Unread is what the new code calls unread.** CONTRACT section 14 has `homes.unread_letters` read a
  `set aside at rollback` marker as unread, so `unread_mail` does too, and such a letter still waits
  for its free beat. `has_mail` and `keeps_rest` keep PR #24's reading (the marker counts as seen),
  which is what the rollback marker is for.
- **"letters wait" is read as `cadence.py` reads it**: anywhere in `REST`'s text, in any case, from a
  regular file only. Only `REST` counts, as the spec says; `EVENT-ONLY` holds no such pace. A linked
  `REST` is never read, so mail still wakes it, and reflect then refuses the link, as in PR #24.
- **guard-restore runs after every beat, whatever `claude`'s exit, before the ledger and the
  commit.** If it fails, `git reset -- CADENCE.md REST EVENT-ONLY inbox` keeps those paths out of the
  commit and they are left for the fleet's tend (after its first tick it restores them). The same
  reset runs on every commit as a second guard; when guard-restore succeeded it is a no-op.
- **`pace_due` keeps the answer it gated on.** CONTRACT section 12 sends `due`'s stdout to
  `/dev/null`; here it is kept in `PACE_DUE` (stderr is still dropped), so reflect learns the beat's
  kind (letter, show-back, schedule or summoned) from the same call that let it through, never from a
  second call that could disagree. `LOVE` wins over `LOVE_DIR` because the launchers set `LOVE`
  without exporting it.
- **The beat's result file is `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/beat-$NAME.XXXXXX"`.** macOS's `mktemp`
  fills only the X's that end a name, so PR #24's `/tmp/beat-$NAME-XXXXXX.json` was the same literal
  name every time: while a file stood there (two beats of one citizen at once, or a beat killed
  before its `rm -f`), `mktemp` failed, `BEAT_JSON` was empty, the redirect failed, no `claude` ran,
  and the ledger took a null cost. The file now has a name of its own each beat, in `$TMPDIR` when
  it is set. If `mktemp` still fails the beat is refused with a plain line, exit 1, never run with
  no file; the `rm -f` stays, and the EXIT trap that releases the lock also removes the file. The
  tests give every beat its own `TMPDIR`, so none of them writes in the shared `/tmp`. Cost: none.
- **`_gates_dir` is made absolute when the file is sourced** (`readlink -f`, then `cd` and `pwd
  -P`), so a script that sourced it by a relative path and then moved into a home still finds
  `citizen_pace.py`. The spend gate's inline Python runs `-I` too, since the beat scripts source it.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Create `tests/test_citizen_pace_shell_gates.py`:

```python
"""The shell gates and citizen-beat.sh's guards (spec section 2 "Markers",
section 3 "The old paid lane", section 7 citizen-gates.sh and citizen-beat.sh;
CONTRACT sections 12 and 14).

keeps_rest, PR #24's marker-only reader, keeps an "asleep, letters wait" REST
asleep with unread mail and still lets mail wake a plain REST. pace_due asks
citizen_pace.py, with the attempt record, and fails toward not due. A beat of
citizen-beat.sh has edit tools, carries no pace paragraph and never shows or
marks a letter, so the script takes the per-citizen lock, refuses a home with
unread mail unless a person summons it, puts the pace files back after every
beat before it commits, and runs its inline Python isolated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import citizen_pace_helpers as h  # noqa: E402

from citizen_pace_lib import attempts, homes, lock, paragraph, tend  # noqa: E402
from citizen_pace_lib import cadence as cad  # noqa: E402
from citizen_pace_lib.cadence import Cadence, SetBy  # noqa: E402
from citizen_pace_lib.words import Pace  # noqa: E402

NOW = "2026-11-20T06:00Z"
OLD = "2026-11-10T06:00Z"            # a last beat ten days before NOW
HOME_MADE = "2026-11-01T00:00Z"
BEAT = h.TOOLS / "citizen-beat.sh"
MINE = SetBy("citizen", "beat", ("2026-11-01T10:00Z",), "pace: asleep")
LETTER = "2026-11-12-hello.md"
PACES = (Pace("asleep-letters-wait"), Pace("asleep"), Pace("listening"), Pace("awake", 5))
# what the beat script prints when it refuses a home with unread mail
LETTERS_WAIT = "has unread mail — letters wait for its free beat"


class Case(h.FixtureCase):
    """Shell runs use the fixture env with PACE_NOW; in-process calls use the
    fixture's git config, never the user's."""

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        keep = ("HOME", "TZ", "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM", "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT")
        patcher = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {k: self.fx.env[k] for k in keep})
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        for k in ("GIT_AUTHOR_NAME", "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL", "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME",
                  "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL", "GIT_AUTHOR_DATE", "GIT_COMMITTER_DATE",
                  "FLEET_BEAT_BOUND_SEC", "BEAT_SUMMONS", "LOVE"):
            os.environ.pop(k, None)
        self.set_now(NOW)
        self.state = self.fx.state
        # each run's TMPDIR, so a beat's scratch file never lands in the shared /tmp
        self.tmp = self.fx.root / "tmp"
        self.tmp.mkdir()

    def env(self, **extra):
        return self.fx.env_at(NOW, **{"TMPDIR": str(self.tmp), **extra})

    def ok(self, r, code=0):
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, code, f"stdout: {r.stdout}\nstderr: {r.stderr}")
        return r

    def gate(self, func, *args):
        return self.fx.gate(func, *args, env=self.env())

    def v2(self, slug, pace, *, last=OLD, letters=(), files=None):
        """A home with a v2 CADENCE.md and markers in step."""
        c = Cadence(slug, 2, pace, MINE, last_beat=last)
        made = {cad.CADENCE: cad.render_cadence(c)}
        for m, text in cad.marker_texts(c).items():
            if text is not None:
                made[m] = text
        made.update(files or {})
        return self.fx.make_home(slug, files=made, letters=letters, when=HOME_MADE,
                                 author=h.beat_author(slug))

    def marker_home(self, slug, pace, *, mail=True):
        """A home holding only the pace's marker (as written by pace/1), and a letter."""
        c = Cadence(slug, 2, pace, MINE)
        files = {m: t for m, t in cad.marker_texts(c).items() if t is not None}
        return self.fx.make_home(slug, files=files, letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")] if mail else ())

    def claude_does(self, body: str) -> None:
        """A fake claude that runs `body` (sh) in the home it is run in, then answers."""
        self.fx.write_bin("claude", '#!/bin/sh\nprintf "%s\\n" "$PWD" >> "$FAKE_CLAUDE_LOG"\n'
                          f'{body}\nprintf "%s" "$FAKE_CLAUDE_OUT"\n')

    def beat(self, slug, script=BEAT, **extra):
        return self.fx.run(script, slug, env=self.env(**extra))

    def committed(self, home, rev="HEAD"):
        """The paths a commit changed."""
        return sorted(self.fx.git(home, "show", "--name-only", "--format=", rev).splitlines())

    def beat_log(self, slug):
        return (self.fx.memory / f"citizen-{slug}.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


# -- keeps_rest and unread_mail ---------------------------------------------------------

class TestKeepsRest(Case):
    def test_letters_wait_rest_keeps_rest_with_unread_mail(self):
        home = self.marker_home("waits", Pace("asleep-letters-wait"))
        self.assertIn("letters wait", (home / "REST").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("has_mail", home).returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 0)

    def test_plain_rest_still_wakes_on_unread_mail(self):
        home = self.marker_home("sleeper", Pace("asleep"))
        self.assertNotIn("letters wait", (home / "REST").read_text(encoding="utf-8").lower())
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 1)
        self.fx.write(home, f"inbox/.seen-{LETTER}", "surfaced 2026-11-19 — shown once, whatever the answer\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 0)

    def test_each_marker_keeps_rest_and_only_letters_wait_holds_against_mail(self):
        for pace in PACES:
            with self.subTest(pace=pace.words()):
                slug = pace.kind.replace("-", "")
                quiet = self.marker_home(f"{slug}q", pace, mail=False)
                self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", quiet).returncode, 0)
                lettered = self.marker_home(f"{slug}m", pace)
                want = 0 if pace.kind == "asleep-letters-wait" else 1
                self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", lettered).returncode, want)

    def test_letters_wait_is_read_in_any_case(self):
        home = self.fx.make_home("shouts", rest="ASLEEP, LETTERS WAIT — by hand only\n",
                                 letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")])
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 0)

    def test_only_rest_says_letters_wait(self):
        home = self.fx.make_home("eventer", event_only="listening — letters wait\n",
                                 letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")])
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 1)

    def test_a_linked_rest_is_never_read(self):
        target = self.fx.outside / "rest-text"
        target.write_text("asleep, letters wait\n", encoding="utf-8")
        home = self.fx.make_home("linked", letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")])
        self.fx.link(home, "REST", target)
        # mail wakes it as before, and reflect then refuses the link
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 1)
        (home / "inbox" / LETTER).unlink()
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 0)

    def test_a_rest_that_is_not_a_regular_file_is_not_opened(self):
        home = self.fx.make_home("piped", letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")])
        os.mkfifo(home / "REST")
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("keeps_rest", home).returncode, 1)   # returns, never blocks


class TestUnreadMail(Case):
    def test_unread_mail_is_has_mail_and_a_letter_set_aside_at_rollback(self):

        self.assertEqual(self.gate("unread_mail", home).returncode, 0)

        home = self.fx.make_home("linkedletter", symlinked_letters=[LETTER])
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("unread_mail", home).returncode, 1)
        elsewhere = self.fx.outside / "letters"
        elsewhere.mkdir()
        (elsewhere / LETTER).write_text("hello\n", encoding="utf-8")
        home = self.fx.make_home("linkedinbox")
        self.fx.link(home, "inbox", elsewhere)
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("unread_mail", home).returncode, 1)
        set_aside = self.fx.outside / "set-aside"
        set_aside.write_text(tend.ROLLBACK_TEXT.format(day="2026-11-19"), encoding="utf-8")
        home = self.fx.make_home("linkedmarker", letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")])
        self.fx.link(home, f"inbox/.seen-{LETTER}", set_aside)
        self.assertEqual(self.gate("unread_mail", home).returncode, 1)    # a linked marker is seen
        self.assertEqual(homes.unread_letters(home), [])


# -- pace_due --------------------------------------------------------------------------

class TestPaceDue(Case):
    SCRIPT = ('. "$1"; shift; pace_due "$@"; rc=$?; printf "%s\\n" "$PACE_DUE"; '
              'pace_reason || echo "-"; exit "$rc"')

    def due_gate(self, home, *flags, gates=h.GATES, env=None, cwd=None, prelude=""):
        """(exit, the JSON due printed or None, pace_reason or '-')."""
        r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", prelude + self.SCRIPT, "_", str(gates), str(home), *flags],
                           env=self.env(**(env or {})), cwd=str(cwd or self.fx.root),
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, check=False)
        lines = r.stdout.splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(len(lines), 2, f"stdout: {r.stdout}\nstderr: {r.stderr}")
        return r.returncode, (json.loads(lines[0]) if lines[0] else None), lines[1]

    def test_a_due_citizen_is_due_with_its_reason(self):
        home = self.v2("waker", Pace("awake", 3))
        rc, d, reason = self.due_gate(home)
        self.assertEqual((rc, reason), (0, "schedule"))
        self.assertEqual((d["due"], d["reason"]), (True, "schedule"))

    def test_a_citizen_not_due_is_not(self):
        home = self.v2("sleeper", Pace("asleep"))
        rc, d, reason = self.due_gate(home)
        self.assertEqual((rc, reason), (1, "no-mail"))
        self.assertFalse(d["due"])

    def test_a_letter_makes_an_asleep_citizen_due(self):
        home = self.v2("reader", Pace("asleep"), letters=[(LETTER, "hello\n")])
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home)[::2], (0, "letter"))

    def test_it_reads_the_attempt_record_in_love_memory(self):
        home = self.v2("waker", Pace("awake", 3))     # CADENCE.md: last beat ten days ago
        attempts.record_outcome(self.state, "waker", "20261119T0600Z-1-1", "silent",
                                "2026-11-19T06:00Z")
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home)[::2], (1, "not-yet"))

    def test_love_set_by_a_launcher_wins_over_love_dir(self):
        home = self.v2("waker", Pace("awake", 3))
        other = self.fx.root / "other-love"
        attempts.record_outcome(other / "memory" / ".fleet-last", "waker", "20261119T0600Z-1-1",
                                "spoken", "2026-11-19T06:00Z")
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home)[::2], (0, "schedule"))
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home, prelude=f'LOVE="{other}"; ')[::2], (1, "not-yet"))

    def test_the_gate_starts_a_clock_once(self):
        home = self.v2("newcomer", Pace("awake", 3), last=None)
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home)[::2], (1, "not-yet"))
        rec = attempts.load(self.state, "newcomer")
        self.assertEqual((rec["last_beat"], rec["seeded"]), (NOW, attempts.SEEDED))
        later = {"PACE_NOW": "2026-11-20T09:00Z"}
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home, env=later)[::2], (1, "not-yet"))
        self.assertEqual(attempts.load(self.state, "newcomer")["last_beat"], NOW)

    def test_a_summons_passes_for_any_pace(self):
        for pace in PACES:
            with self.subTest(pace=pace.words()):
                home = self.v2(pace.kind.replace("-", ""), pace, last="2026-11-19T06:00Z")
                self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home)[0], 1)
                self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home, "--summoned")[::2], (0, "summoned"))

    def test_any_error_is_not_due(self):
        home = self.v2("waker", Pace("awake", 3))
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(home)[0], 0)
        cases = {"missing": None,
                 "crashing": "raise RuntimeError('broken')\n",
                 "erroring": "import sys\nprint('{\"due\": true}')\nsys.exit(2)\n"}
        for name, source in cases.items():
            with self.subTest(citizen_pace_py=name):
                tools = self.fx.root / f"tools-{name}"
                tools.mkdir()
                shutil.copy(h.GATES, tools / "citizen-gates.sh")
                if source is not None:
                    (tools / "citizen_pace.py").write_text(source, encoding="utf-8")
                rc, _d, reason = self.due_gate(home, gates=tools / "citizen-gates.sh")
                self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
                if name != "erroring":
                    self.assertEqual(reason, "-")
        not_a_home = self.fx.root / "not-a-citizen"
        not_a_home.mkdir()
        self.assertEqual(self.due_gate(not_a_home)[0], 1)

    def test_it_runs_isolated_from_any_folder(self):
        home = self.v2("waker", Pace("awake", 3))
        canary = self.fx.outside / "imported"
        trap = f"open({str(canary)!r}, 'w').write('imported')\n"
        self.fx.write(home, "json.py", trap)
        self.fx.write(home, "urllib/__init__.py", trap)
        # the gates sourced by a relative path, then the caller moves into the home
        script = ('. tools/citizen-gates.sh; cd "$1"; pace_due "$1"; rc=$?; '
                  'pace_reason; exit "$rc"')
        r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script, "_", str(home)], env=self.env(),
                           cwd=str(h.ROOT), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60,
                           check=False)
        self.assertEqual((r.returncode, r.stdout), (0, "schedule\n"), r.stderr)
        self.assertFalse(canary.exists())


class TestSpendGateIsolated(Case):
    def test_the_spend_gate_imports_nothing_from_the_folder_it_runs_in(self):
        folder = self.fx.root / "cwd"
        canary = self.fx.outside / "imported"
        trap = f"open({str(canary)!r}, 'w').write('imported')\n"
        for name in ("json.py", "math.py"):

        ledger = self.fx.memory / "fleet-economy.jsonl"

        script = '. "$1"; spent_today "$2"; budget_reached "$2" 1.50 && echo reached || echo under'
        r = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script, "_", str(h.GATES), str(ledger)], env=self.env(),
                           cwd=str(folder), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60, check=False)
        self.assertEqual(r.stdout, "0.2500\nunder\n", r.stderr)
        self.assertFalse(canary.exists())


# -- citizen-beat.sh: the lock ----------------------------------------------------------

class TestBeatLock(Case):
    def test_it_holds_the_lock_through_the_beat_and_releases_it(self):
        self.fx.make_home("waker")
        seen = self.fx.root / "lock-seen"
        lockdir = self.state / "waker.lock"
        self.claude_does(f'cat "{lockdir}/pid" > "{seen}" 2>/dev/null')
        self.ok(self.beat("waker"))
        self.assertEqual(self.fx.claude_calls(), ["citizen-waker"])
        self.assertTrue(seen.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip().isdigit())
        self.assertFalse(os.path.lexists(lockdir))

    def test_a_held_lock_means_busy_and_no_beat(self):
        self.fx.make_home("waker")
        self.assertTrue(lock.take(self.state, "waker", os.getpid()).got)   # a live holder: this test
        r = self.ok(self.beat("waker"))
        self.assertIn(f"waker: its lock is held by pid {os.getpid()}, started {NOW} — busy, no beat",
                      r.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.fx.claude_calls(), [])
        self.assertEqual(lock.holder(self.state, "waker").pid, os.getpid())
        self.assertIsNone(attempts.load(self.state, "waker")["attempt"])   # a hand-run writes none

    def test_a_stale_lock_is_reclaimed_and_logged(self):
        self.fx.make_home("waker")
        gone = subprocess.Popen(["/usr/bin/true"])
        gone.wait()
        self.assertTrue(lock.take(self.state, "waker", gone.pid).got)
        r = self.ok(self.beat("waker"))
        self.assertIn(f"waker: a stale lock was reclaimed (pid {gone.pid} is gone)", r.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.fx.claude_calls(), ["citizen-waker"])
        self.assertFalse(os.path.lexists(self.state / "waker.lock"))

    def test_a_lock_that_cannot_be_taken_refuses_the_beat(self):
        self.fx.make_home("waker")
        self.state.write_text("not a folder\n", encoding="utf-8")
        r = self.ok(self.beat("waker"), 1)
        self.assertIn("waker's lock could not be taken — beat refused", r.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(self.fx.claude_calls(), [])

    def test_halt_takes_no_lock(self):
        self.fx.make_home("waker")
        (self.fx.love / "HALT").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
        self.ok(self.beat("waker"))
        self.assertFalse(os.path.lexists(self.state / "waker.lock"))
        self.assertEqual(self.fx.claude_calls(), [])
```
